8.8.d: बृह॒द् धि॒ जा॒लं बृहतः॒ शक्र॒स्य वाजि॒नीवतः । ते॒न श॒त्रून् अभि॒ स॒र्वान् न्य् उ॑ब्ज य॒था न॒ मु॒च्यातै कतम॒श् चनै॒षाम् ॥६॥
8.8.e: Verily mighty is the net of mighty Sakra rich in wealth: Therewith press all the foemen down so that not one of them escape!

8.8.d: बृह॒त् ते जा॒लं बृहत॒ इन्द्र शूर सहस्रार्घ॒स्य शत॒वीर्यस्य । ते॒न शतं॒ सह॒स्रम् अयु॒तं न्य॑र्बुदं जघा॒न शक्रो॒ द॒स्यूनाम् अभिधा॒य से॒नया ॥७॥
8.8.e: Great is thy net, brave Indra, thine the mighty match for a thousand, Lord of Hundred Powers! Holding them, with his host, therewith hath Indra slaughtered Dasyus a hundred, thousand, myriad, hundred millions.

8.8.d: अयं॒ लोको॒ जा॒लम् आसीच् छक्र॒स्य महतो॒ महा॒न् । ते॒नाह॒म् इन्द्रजाले॒नामूं॒स् त॒मसाभि॒ दधामि स॒र्वान् ॥८॥
8.8.e: This world so mighty was the net of Sakra, of the Mighty One: With this, the net of Indra, I envelop all those men with gloom.

8.8.d: सेदि॒र् उग्रा॒ व्यृ॑द्धिर् आ॒र्तिश् चानपवाचना॒ । श्र॒मस् तन्द्री॒श् च मो॒हश् च तै॒र् अमू॒न् अभि॒ दधामि स॒र्वान् ॥९॥
8.8.e: Great weakness and misfortune, pain which words can never charm away, Languor, fatigue, bewilderment, with these I compass all the foes.

8.8.d: मृत्य॒वे ऽमू॒न् प्र॒ यछामि मृत्युपाशै॒र् अमी॒ सिताः॒ । मृत्यो॒र् ये॒ अघला॒ दूता॒स् ते॒भ्य एनान् प्र॒ति नयामि बद्ध्वा॒ ॥१०॥ {२०}
8.8.e: I give those foemen up to Death: bound in the bonds of Death are they. I bind and carry them away to meet Death's wicked messengers.

8.8.d: न॒यतामू॒न् मृत्युदूता य॒मदूता अ॒पोम्भत । परःसहस्रा॒ हन्यन्तां तृणे॒ढ्व् एनान् मत्यं॑ भव॒स्य ॥११॥
8.8.e: Bear them away, Death's messengers! envoys of Yama! bind them fast. More than a thousand be their slain: the club of Bhava pierce them through!

8.8.d: साध्या॒ ए॒कं जालदण्ड॒म् उद्य॒त्य यन्त्य् ओ॒जसा । रुद्रा॒ ए॒कं व॒सव ए॒कम् आदित्यै॒र् ए॒क उ॒द्यतः ॥१२॥
8.8.e: Forth go the Sādhyas in their might bearing one netpole raised aloft. One pole the Rudras carry, one the Vasus, and the Ādityas one.

8.8.d: वि॒श्वे देवाः॒ उप॒रिष्टाद् उब्ज॒न्तो यन्त्व् ओ॒जसा । म॒ध्येन घ्न॒न्तो यन्तु से॒नाम् अ॒ङ्गिरसो मही॒म् ॥१३॥
8.8.e: The Visve Devas from above shall come depressing it with might, And in the midst the Angirases, slaying the mighty host, shall go.

8.8.d: व॒नस्प॒तीन् वानस्पत्या॒न् ओ॒षधीर् उत॒ वीरु॒धः । द्विपा॒च् च॒तुष्पाद् इष्णामि य॒था से॒नाम् अमूं॒ ह॒नन् ॥१४॥
8.8.e: Trees of the forest, trees that bear flower and fruit, and herbs and plants, Quadruped, biped send I forth that they may strike this army dead,

8.8.d: गन्धर्वाप्सर॒सः सर्पा॒न् देवा॒न् पुण्यजना॒न् पितृ॒̄न् । दृष्टा॒न् अदृ॒ष्टान् इष्णामि य॒था से॒नाम् अमूं॒ ह॒नन् ॥१५॥
8.8.e: Gandharvas, and Apsarases, Gods, Serpents, Fathers, Holy Men, Seen and unseen, I send them forth that they may strike this army dead.

8.8.d: इम॒ उप्ता॒ मृत्युपाशा॒ या॒न् आक्र॒म्य न॒ मुच्य॒से । अमु॒ष्या हन्तु से॒नाया इदं॒ कू॒टं सहस्रशः॒ ॥१६॥
8.8.e: Here spread are snares of Death wherefrom thou, once within them, ne'er art freed: Full many a thousand of the host yonder this horn shall smite and slay.

8.8.d: घर्मः॒ स॒मिद्धो अग्नि॒नायं॒ हो॒मः सहस्रहः॒ । भव॒श् च पृ॒श्निबाहुश् च श॒र्व से॒नाम् अमूं॒ हतम् ॥१७॥
8.8.e: The Gharma hath been warmed with fire: this Homa slays a thousand men. Let Bhava, Prisnibāhu, and Sarva destroy that armament.

8.8.d: मृत्यो॒र् आ॒षम् आ॒ पद्यन्तां क्षु॒धं सेदिं॒ वध॒म् भय॒म् । इ॒न्द्रश् चाक्षुजाला॒भ्यां श॒र्व से॒नाम् अमूं॒ हतम् ॥१८॥
8.8.e: Their portion be the fire of Death, hunger, exhaustion, slaughter, fear. With your entangling snares and nets, Sarva and Indra! slay that host.

8.8.d: प॒राजिताः प्र॒ त्रसतामित्रा नुत्ता॒ धावत ब्र॒ह्मणा । बृ॒हस्प॒तिप्रनुत्तानां मा॒मी॒षां मोचि क॒श् चन॒ ॥१९॥
8.8.e: Fly, conquered, in alarm, ye foes, run driven by the spell away! Let not one man escape of those when routed by Brihaspati.

8.8.d: अ॒व पद्यन्ताम् एषाम् आ॒युधानि मा॒ शकन् प्रतिधा॒म् इ॒षुम् । अ॒थैषां बहु॒ बि॒भ्यताम् इ॒षवः घ्नन्तु म॒र्मणि ॥२०॥
8.8.e: Down fall their weapons on the ground: no strength be theirs to point a shaft: Then in their dreadful terror let their arrows wound their vital parts.

8.8.d: सं॒ क्रोशताम् एनान् द्या॒वापृथिवी॒ स॒म् अन्त॒रिक्षं सह॒ देव॒ताभिः । मा॒ ज्ञाता॒रं मा॒ प्रतिष्ठां॒ विदन्त मिथो॒ विघ्नाना॒ उ॒प यन्तु मृत्यु॒म् ॥२१॥
8.8.e: Let Heaven and Earth roar out in wrath against them, and Air with all the Deities in concert, Let them not find a surety or a refuge, but torn away go down to Death together.

8.8.d: दि॒शश् च॒तस्रो ऽश्वतर्यो॑ देवरथ॒स्य पुरोदा॒शाः शफा॒ अन्त॒रिक्षम् उद्धिः॒ । द्या॒वापृथिवी॒ प॒क्षसी ऋत॒वो ऽभी॒शवो ऽन्तर्देशाः॒ किम्करा॒ वा॒क् प॒रिरथ्यम् ॥२२॥
8.8.e: The mules of the Gods' car are heaven's four quarters; their hooves are sacred cakes, the air its body. Its sides are Heaven and Earth, its reins the Seasons, Voice is its hood, its grooms are sky's mid-regions.

8.8.d: संवत्सरो॒ र॒थः परिवत्सरो॒ रथोपस्थो॒ विरा॒ड् ईषा॒ग्नी॒ रथमुख॒म् । इ॒न्द्रः सव्यष्ठा॒श् चन्द्र॒माः सा॒रथिः ॥२३॥
8.8.e: Year is the car, Full Year the seat for driving, Virāj the pole, the chariot's front is Agni, Indra the warrior, and the Moon the driver.

8.8.d: इतो॒ जयेतो॒ वि॒ जय सं॒ जय ज॒य स्वा॒हा । इमे॒ जयन्तु प॒रामी॒ जयन्तां स्वा॒हैभ्यो॒ दुरा॒हामी॒भ्यः । नीललोहिते॒नामू॒न् अभ्य॒वतनोमि ॥२४॥ {२१}
8.8.e: Hence conquer, conquer, Hail! be thou the victor! Let these be conquerors and those be conquered. Good luck to these, ill luck to those men yonder! With the dark-blue-and-red our foes I cover.

8.9.d: कु॒तस् तौ॒ जातौ॒ कतमः॒ सो॒ अ॒र्धः क॒स्माल् लोका॒त् कतम॒स्याः पृथिव्याः॒ । वत्सौ॒ विरा॒जः सलिला॒द् उ॒द् ऐतां तौ॒ त्वा पृछामि कतरे॒ण दुग्धा॒ ॥१॥
8.9.e: Whence were these two produced? which was that region?' From what world, from which earth had they their being? Calves of Virāj, these two arose from water. I ask thee of these twain, who was their milker.

8.9.d: यो॒ अ॒क्रन्दयत् सलिलं॒ महित्वा॒ यो॒निं कृत्वा॒ त्रिभु॒जं श॒यानः । वत्सः॒ कामदु॒घो विरा॒जः स॒ गु॒हा चक्रे तन्वः॑ पराचैः॒ ॥२॥
8.9.e: He who prepared a threefold home, and lying there made the water bellow through his greatness, Calf of Virāj, giving each wish fulfilment, made bodies for him- self far off, in secret.

8.9.d: या॒नि त्री॒णि बृह॒न्ति ये॒षां चतुर्थं॒ वियुन॒क्ति वा॒चम् । ब्रह्मै॒नद् विद्यात् त॒पसा विपश्चि॒द् य॒स्मिन्न् ए॒कं युज्य॒ते य॒स्मिन्न् ए॒कम् ॥३॥
8.9.e: Which are the three, the mighty three, whereof the fourth divides the voice, This may the Brāhman know by prayer and fervour, whereto belongs the one, whereto the other.

8.9.d: बृहतः॒ प॒रि सा॒मानि षष्ठा॒त् प॒ञ्चा॒धि नि॒र्मिता । बृह॒द् बृहत्या॒ नि॒र्मितं कु॒तो॒ ऽधि बृहती॒ मिता॒ ॥४॥
8.9.e: Out of the Brihat as the sixth five Salmons have been fashioned forth: From Brihatī was Brihat formed: whence was the Brihatī com- posed?

8.9.d: बृहती॒ प॒रि मा॒त्राया मातु॒र् मा॒त्रा॒धि नि॒र्मिता । माया॒ ह जज्ञे माया॒या माया॒या मा॒तली प॒रि ॥५॥
8.9.e: On measure Brihatī is based, and measure on the measurer: From magic might came magic might, from magic might came Mātali.

8.9.d: वैश्वानर॒स्य प्रतिमो॒प॒रि द्यौ॒र् या॒वद् रो॒दसी विबबाधे॒ अग्निः॒ । त॒तः षष्ठा॒द् आ॒मु॒तो यन्ति स्तो॒मा उ॒द् इतो॒ यन्त्य् अभि॒ षष्ठ॒म् अ॒ह्नः ॥६॥
8.9.e: Vaisvānara's image is the sky above us, so far as Agni forced both spheres asunder. Thence from that region as the sixth come praise-songs, and every sixth day hence again go upward.

8.9.d: ष॒ट् त्वा पृछाम ऋ॒षयः कश्यपेमे॒ त्वं॒ हि॒ युक्तं॒ युयुक्षे॒ यो॒ग्यं च । विरा॒जम् आहुर् ब्र॒ह्मणः पित॒रं तां॒ नो वि॒ धेहि यतिधा॒ स॒खिभ्यः ॥७॥
8.9.e: We, Kagyapa! six present Rishis, ask thee—for thou hast prov- ed things tried and meet for trial They call Virāj the Father of Devotion: tell her to us thy friends in all her figures.

8.9.d: यां॒ प्र॒च्युताम् अ॒नु यज्ञाः॒ प्रच्य॒वन्त उपति॒ष्ठन्त उपति॒ष्ठमानाम् । य॒स्या व्रते॒ प्रसवे॒ यक्ष॒म् ए॒जति सा॒ विरा॒ट् ऋषयः परमे॒ व्यो॑मन् ॥८॥
8.9.e: She whom, advancing, sacrifices follow, and when she takes her station stand beside her, By whose control and hest the spirit moveth, she is Virāj, in highest heaven, O Rishis.

8.9.d: अप्राणै॒ति प्राणे॒न प्राणती॒नां विरा॒ट् स्वरा॒जम् अभ्य् ए॑ति पश्चा॒त् । वि॒श्वं मृश॒न्तीम् अभि॒रूपां विरा॒जं प॒श्यन्ति त्वे॒ न त्वे॒ पश्यन्त्य् एनाम् ॥९॥
8.9.e: Breathless, she moves by breath of living creatures, Svarāj pre- cedes, Virāj comes closely after. Some men behold her not, and some behold her, Virāj meet- shaped, who thinks of all existence.

8.9.d: को॒ विरा॒जो मिथुनत्वं॒ प्र॒ वेद क॒ ऋतू॒न् क॒ उ क॒ल्पम् अस्याः । क्र॒मान् को॒ अस्याः कतिधा॒ वि॒दुग्धान् को॒ अस्या धा॒म कतिधा॒ व्यु॑ष्टीः ॥१०॥ {२२}
8.9.e: Who hath perceived Virāj's duplication, perceived her seasons and her rule and practice? Who knows her steps, how oft, how far extended, who knows her home and number of her dawnings?

8.9.d: इय॒म् एव॒ सा॒ या॒ प्रथमा॒ व्यौ॒छद् आस्व् इ॒तरासु चरति प्र॒विष्टा । महा॒न्तो अस्यां महिमा॒नो अन्त॒र् वधू॒र् जिगाय नवग॒ज् ज॒नित्री ॥११॥
8.9.e: She here who first of all sent forth her lustre moves onward resting on these lower creatures. Exalted power and might are stored within her: the woman hath prevailed, the new-come mother.

8.9.d: छ॒न्दःपक्षे उष॒सा पे॒पिशाने समानं॒ यो॒निम् अ॒नु सं॒ चरेमे । सू॒र्यपत्नी सं॒ चरतः प्रजानती॒ केतुम॒ती अज॒रे भू॒रिरेतसा ॥१२॥
8.9.e: Both Dawns on wings of song, with rich adornment, move on together to their common dwelling. Sūrya's two wives, unwasting, most prolific, knowing their way, move, rich in light, together.

8.9.d: ऋत॒स्य प॒न्थाम् अ॒नु तिस्र॒ आ॒गुस् त्र॒यो घर्मा॒ अ॒नु रे॒त आ॒गुः । प्रजा॒म् ए॒का जि॒न्वत्य् ऊ॒र्जम् ए॒का राष्ट्र॒म् ए॒का रक्षति देवयूना॒म् ॥१३॥
8.9.e: The three have passed along the path of Order—three warm libations have regarded offspring One quickens progeny, one strengthens vigour, and one protects the kingdom of the pious.

8.9.d: अग्नी॒षो॒माव् अदधुर् या॒ तुरी॒या॒सीद् यज्ञ॒स्य पक्षा॒व् ऋ॒षयः कल्प॒यन्तः । गायत्रीं॒ त्रिष्टु॒भं ज॒गतीम् अनुष्टु॒भं बृहदर्कीं॒ य॒जमानाय स्व॑र् आभ॒रन्तीम् ॥१४॥
8.9.e: She who was fourth was made by Agni, Soma, and Rishis as. they formed both halves of worship, Gāyatrī, Trishtup, Jagatī, Anushtup, Brihadarki lightening the sacrificer.

8.9.d: प॒ञ्च व्यु॑ष्टीर् अ॒नु प॒ञ्च दो॒हा गां॒ प॒ञ्चनाम्नीम् ऋत॒वो॒ ऽनु प॒ञ्च । प॒ञ्च दि॒शः पञ्चदशे॒न क्ल्̥प्ता॒स् ता॒ ए॒कमूर्ध्नीर् अभि॒ लोक॒म् ए॒कम् ॥१५॥
8.9.e: Five milkings answer to the fivefold dawning, five seasons to the cow who bears five titles. The five sky-regions made fifteen in number, one head have these to one sole world directed.

8.9.d: ष॒ट् जाता॒ भूता॒ प्रथमजा॒ ऋत॒स्य ष॒ट् उ सा॒मानि षटहं॒ वहन्ति । षट्योगं॒ सी॒रम् अ॒नु सा॒मसाम ष॒ट् आहुर् द्या॒वापृथिवीः॒ ष॒ट् उर्वीः॒ ॥१६॥
8.9.e: Six Elements arose, first-born of Order: the six-day time is carried by six Sāmans. Six-yoked the plough is, as each trace is numbered: they call both broad ones six; six, Earth and Heaven.

8.9.d: ष॒ड् आहुः शीता॒न् ष॒ड् उ मास॒ उष्णा॒न् ऋतुं॒ नो ब्रू॒त यतमो॒ ऽतिरिक्तः । सप्त॒ सुपर्णाः॒ कव॒यो नि॒ षेदुः सप्त॒ छ॒न्दांस्य् अ॒नु सप्त॒ दीक्षाः॒ ॥१७॥
8.9.e: They call the cold months six, and six the hot ones. Which, tell us, of the seasons is redundant? Seven sages, eagles, have sat down together: seven metres match the seven Consecrations.

8.9.d: सप्त॒ हो॒माः समि॒धो ह सप्त॒ म॒धूनि सप्त॒ ऋत॒वो ह सप्त॒ । सप्ता॒ज्यानि प॒रि भूत॒म् आयन् ताः॒ सप्तगृध्रा॒ इ॒ति शुश्रुमा वय॒म् ॥१८॥
8.9.e: Seven are the Homas, seven the logs for burning, seven are the streams of mead, and seven the seasons. Into the world have come seven streams of butter; those we have heard of as the Seven Vultures.

8.9.d: सप्त॒ छ॒न्दांसि चतुरुत्तरा॒ण्य् अन्यो॒ अन्य॒स्मिन्न् अ॒ध्य् आ॒र्पितानि । कथं॒ स्तो॒माः प्र॒ति तिष्ठन्ति ते॒षु ता॒नि स्तो॒मेषु कथ॒म् आ॒र्पितानि ॥१९॥
8.9.e: Seven metres, by four syllables increasing, each of the seven founded upon another How are the hymns of praise on these supported, and how are these imposed upon the praise-songs?

8.9.d: कथं॒ गायत्री॒ त्रिवृ॒तं व्य् आ॑प कथं॒ त्रिष्टु॒प् पञ्चदशे॒न कल्पते । त्रयस्त्रिंशे॒न ज॒गती कथ॒म् अनुष्टु॒प् कथ॒म् एकविंशः॒ ॥२०॥ {२३}
8.9.e: How hath the Gāyatri filled out three triads? On the fifteen how is the Trishtup moulded, Jagatī fashioned on the three-and-thirty? How is Anushtup formed? how Ekavinsa?

8.9.d: अष्ट॒ जाता॒ भूता॒ प्रथमजा॒ ऋत॒स्याष्टे॒न्द्र ऋत्वि॒जो दै॒व्या ये॒ । अष्ट॒योनिर् अ॒दितिर् अष्ट॒पुत्रास्तमीं॒ रा॒त्रिम् अभि॒ हव्य॒म् एति ॥२१॥
8.9.e: Eight Elements sprang up, first born of Order: the Priests divine are eight in number, Indra! Eight are the wombs of Aditi, eight her children; for the eighth night is the libation destined.

8.9.d: इत्थं॒ श्रे॒यो म॒न्यमानेद॒म् आ॒गमं युष्मा॒कं सख्ये॒ अह॒म् अस्मि शे॒वा । समान॒जन्मा क्र॒तुर् अस्ति वः॒ शिवः॒ स॒ वः स॒र्वाः सं॒ चरति प्रजान॒न् ॥२२॥
8.9.e: So planning bliss for you have I come hither to win your friendship: kind am I, and gracious. Born from one source, propitious is your wisdom: knowing full well to all of you it cometh.

8.9.d: अष्टे॒न्द्रस्य ष॒ड् यम॒स्य ऋ॒षीणां सप्त॒ सप्तधा॒ । अपो॒ मनुष्या॑न् ओ॒षधीस् तां॒ उ प॒ञ्चा॒नु सेचिरे ॥२३॥
8.9.e: To Indra eight, to Yama six, seven to the Rishis, seven to each: The number five accompanies waters and men and healing herbs.

8.9.d: के॒वली॒न्द्राय दुदुहे॒ हि॒ गृष्टि॒र् व॒शम् पीयू॒षं प्रथमं॒ दु॒हाना । अ॒थातर्पयच् चतु॒रश् चतुर्धा॒ देवा॒न् मनुष्यां॑ अ॒सुरान् उत॒ ऋ॒षीन् ॥२४॥
8.9.e: The Heifer, all his own, poured forth for Indra control and milk at her first time of milking; And he then satisfied the four divisions, the Gods and men and Asuras and Rishis.

8.9.d: को॒ नु॒ गौः॒ क॒ एकऋषिः॒ कि॒म् उ धा॒म का॒ आशि॒षः । यक्ष॒म् पृथिव्या॒म् एकवृ॒द् एकर्तुः॒ कतमो॒ नु॒ सः॒ ॥२५॥
8.9.e: Who is the Cow? Who is the Single Rishi? What is the law, what are the benedictions? What on the earth is the one only Spirit? Which of the number is the Single Season?

8.9.d: एको॒ गौ॒र् ए॒क एकऋषि॒र् ए॒कं धा॒मैकधा॒शि॒षः । यक्षं॒ पृथिव्या॒म् एकवृ॒द् एकर्तु॒र् ना॒ति रिच्यते ॥२६॥ {२४}
8.9.e: One is the Cow, one is the Single Spirit, one is the law, single are benedictions. The Spirit dwelling on the earth is single: the Single Season never is transcended.

8.10.d: विरा॒ड् वा॒ इद॒म् अ॒ग्र आसीत् त॒स्या जाता॒याः स॒र्वम् अबिभेद् इय॒म् एवे॒दं॒ भविष्य॒ती॒ति ॥१॥
8.10.e: Viraj at first was This. At birth all feared her; the thought, She will become this All, struck terror.

8.10.d: सो॒द् अक्रामत् सा॒ गा॒र्हपत्ये न्य् अ॑क्रामत् । गृहमेधी॒ गृह॒पतिर् भवति य॒ एवं॒ वे॒द ॥२॥
8.10.e: She rose, the Gārhapatya fire she entered. He who knows this becomes lord of a household, performer of domestic sacri- fices.

8.10.d: सो॒द् अक्रामत् सा॒हवनी॒ये न्य् अ॑क्रामत् । य॒न्त्य् अस्य देवा॒ देव॒हूतिं प्रियो॒ देवा॒नां भवति य॒ एवं॒ वे॒द ॥३॥
8.10.e: She mounted up, the Eastward fire she entered. He who knows this becomes the Gods' beloved, and to his call they come when she invokes them.

8.10.d: सो॒द् अक्रामत् सा॒ दक्षिणाग्नौ॒ न्य् अ॑क्रामत् । यज्ञ॒र्तो दक्षिणी॒यो वा॒सतेयो भवति य॒ एवं॒ वे॒द ॥४॥
8.10.e: She mounted up, the Southward fire she entered. He who knows this becomes a fit performer of sacrifice, meet for honour, shelter-giver.

8.10.d: सो॒द् अक्रामत् सा॒ सभा॒यां न्य् अ॑क्रामत् । य॒न्त्य् अस्य सभां॒ स॒भ्यो भवति य॒ एवं॒ वे॒द ॥५॥
8.10.e: She mounted up, she entered the Assembly. He who knows this becomes polite and courtly, and people come as guests to his assembly.

8.10.d: सो॒द् अक्रामत् सा॒ स॒मितौ न्य् अ॑क्रामत् । य॒न्त्य् अस्य स॒मितिं सामित्यो॒ भवति य॒ एवं॒ वे॒द ॥६॥
8.10.e: She mounted up, she passed within the meeting. He who knows this becomes fit for the meeting, and to his hall of meeting come the people.

8.10.d: सो॒द् अक्रामत् सा॒म॒न्त्रणे न्य् अ॑क्रामत् । य॒न्त्य् अस्याम॒न्त्रणम् आमन्त्रणी॒यो भवति य॒ एवं॒ वे॒द ॥७॥ {२५}
8.10.e: She mounted up, she entered Consultation. Whoso knows this is fit to be consulted, and to his consultation come the people.

8.10.d: सो॒द् अक्रामत् सा॒न्त॒रिक्षे चतुर्धा॒ वि॒क्रान्तातिष्ठत् ॥८॥
8.10.e: She mounted up, and, into four divided, she took her station in the air's mid-region.

8.10.d: तां॒ देवमनुष्या॑ अब्रुवन्न् इय॒म् एव॒ त॒द् वेद य॒द् उभ॒य उपजी॒वेमेमा॒म् उ॒प ह्वयामहा इ॒ति ॥९॥
8.10.e: Of her the Gods and men said, This she knoweth. That we may both have life let us invoke her.

8.10.d: ता॒म् उ॒पाह्वयन्त ॥१०॥
8.10.e: Thus did they cry to her:

8.10.d: ऊ॒र्ज ए॒हि स्व॒ध एहि सू॒नृत ए॒ही॒रावत्य् ए॒ही॒ति ॥११॥
8.10.e: Come, Strength! come, Food! come, Charmer! come, Free- giver!

8.10.d: त॒स्या इ॒न्द्रो वत्स॒ आ॒सीद् गायत्र्य् अ॑भिधा॒न्य् अभ्र॒म् ऊ॒धः ॥१२॥
8.10.e: Her calf, her well-beloved calf, was Indra: Gāyatri was her rope, the cloud her udder.

8.10.d: बृह॒च् च रथंतरं॒ च द्वौ॒ स्त॒नाव् आ॒स्तां यज्ञायज्ञि॒यं च वामदेव्यं॒ च द्वौ॒ ॥१३॥
8.10.e: Two teats she had, Rathantara and Brihat, two, Yajnāyajniya and Vāmadevya.

8.10.d: ओ॒षधीर् एव॒ रथंतरे॒ण देवा॒ अदुह्रन् व्य॒चो बृह॒ता ॥१४॥
8.10.e: With the Rathantara the Gods milked from her the Plants, and all the wide expanse with Brihat.

8.10.d: अपो॒ वामदेव्ये॒न यज्ञं॒ यज्ञायज्ञि॒येन ॥१५॥
8.10.e: They drew the Waters forth with Vāmadevya, with Yajnayaj- niya they milked out worship.

8.10.d: ओ॒षधीर् एवा॒स्मै रथंतरं॒ दुहे व्य॒चो बृह॒त् ॥१६॥
8.10.e: For him who knoweth this, Rathantara poureth out Plants, and Brihat yieldeth wide expansion.

8.10.d: अपो॒ वामदेव्यं॒ यज्ञं॒ यज्ञायज्ञि॒यं य॒ वे॒द ॥१७॥ {२६}
8.10.e: Waters from Vāmdevya come, from Yajnāyajniya sacrifice.

8.10.d: सो॒द् अक्रामत् सा॒ व॒नस्प॒तीन् आ॒गछत् तां॒ व॒नस्प॒तयो ऽघ्नत सा॒ संवत्सरे॒ स॒म् अभवत् । त॒स्माद् व॒नस्प॒तीनां संवत्सरे॒ वृक्ण॒म् अ॒पि रोहति वृश्च॒ते ऽस्या॒प्रियो भ्रा॒तृव्यो य॒ एवं॒ वे॒द ॥१८॥
8.10.e: She rose, she came unto the tress: they killed her. A year went by and she again existed. Hence in a year the wounds of trees heal over. He who knows this sees his loathed rival wounded.

8.10.d: सो॒द् अक्रामत् सा॒ पितृ॒̄न् आ॒गछत् तां॒ पित॒रो ऽघ्नत सा॒ मासि॒ स॒म् अभवत् । त॒स्मात् पितृ॒भ्यो मास्य् उ॒पमास्यं ददति प्र॒ पितृया॒णं प॒न्थां जानाति य॒ एवं॒ वे॒द ॥१९॥
8.10.e: She mounted up, she came unto the Fathers: they killed her: in a month she re-existed. Hence men give monthly offerings to the Fathers: who knows this, knows the path which they have trodden.

8.10.d: सो॒द् अक्रामत् सा॒ देवा॒न् आ॒गछत् तां॒ देवा॒ अघ्नत सा॒र्धमासे॒ स॒म् अभवत् । त॒स्माद् देवे॒भ्यो ऽर्धमासे॒ व॒षट् कुर्वन्ति प्र॒ देवया॒नं प॒न्थां जानाति य॒ एवं॒ वे॒द ॥२०॥
8.10.e: She rose, she came unto the Gods: they killed her: but in a fortnight she again was living. Fortnightly, hence, men serve the Gods with Vasat! Who knows this knows the way which Gods pass over.

8.10.d: सो॒द् अक्रामत् सा॒ मनुष्या॑न् आ॒गछत् तां॒ मनुष्या॑ अघ्नत सा॒ सद्यः॒ स॒म् अभवत् । त॒स्मान् मनुष्ये॑भ्य उभयद्यु॒र् उ॒प हरन्त्य् उ॒पास्य गृहे॒ हरन्ति य॒ एवं॒ वे॒द ॥२१॥ {२७}
8.10.e: She mounted up, she came to men: they killed her Presently she regained her life and being. Hence on both days to men they bring and offer—who knows this—near-seated in the dwelling.

8.10.d: सो॒द् अक्रामत् सा॒सुरान् आ॒गछत् ता॒म् अ॒सुरा उ॒पाह्वयन्त मा॒य ए॒ही॒ति । त॒स्या विरो॒चनः प्रा॒ह्रादिर् वत्स॒ आ॒सीद् अयस्पात्रं॒ पा॒त्रम् । तां॒ द्वि॒मूर्धार्त्व्यो॑ ऽधोक् तां॒ माया॒म् एवा॒धोक् ॥ तां॒ माया॒म् अ॒सुरा उ॒प जीवन्त्य् उपजीवनी॒यो भवति य॒ एवं॒ वे॒द ॥२२॥
8.10.e: She rose, approached the Asuras: they called her: their cry was, Come, O Māyā, come thou hither. Her dear calf was Virochana Prāhrādi: her milking vessel was a. pan of iron. Dvimūrdhā Ārtvya milked her, yea, this Māyā, The Asuras depend for life on Māyā. He who knows this becomes a fit supporter.

8.10.d: सो॒द् अक्रामत् सा॒ पितृ॒̄न् आ॒गछत् तां॒ पित॒र उ॒पाह्वयन्त स्व॒ध ए॒ही॒ति । त॒स्या यमो॒ रा॒जा वत्स॒ आ॒सीद् रजतपात्रं॒ पा॒त्रम् । ता॒म् अ॒न्तको मार्त्यवो॒ ऽधोक् तां॒ स्वधा॒म् एवा॒धोक् । तां॒ स्वधां॒ पित॒र उ॒प जीवन्त्य् उपजीवनी॒यो भवति य॒ एवं॒ वे॒द ॥२३॥
8.10.e: She mounted up, she came unto the Fathers. The Fathers called. to her, O Food, come hither. King Yama was her calf, her pail was silvern. Antaka, Mrityu's. son, milked her, this Svadhā. This Food the Fathers make their lives' sustainer. He who knows this becomes a meet supporter.

8.10.d: सो॒द् अक्रामत् सा॒ मनुष्या॑न् आ॒गछत् तां॒ मनुष्या॑ उ॒पाह्वयन्ते॒रावत्य् ए॒ही॒ति । त॒स्या म॒नुर् वैवस्वतो॒ वत्स॒ आ॒सीत् पृथिवी॒ पा॒त्रम् । तां॒ पृ॒थी वैन्यो॑ ऽधोक् तां॒ कृषिं॒ च सस्यं॒ चाधोक् । ते॒ स्वधां॒ कृषिं॒ च सस्यं॒ च मनुष्या॑ उ॒प जीवन्ति कृष्ट॒राधिर् उपजीवनी॒यो भवति य॒ एवं॒ वे॒द ॥२४॥
8.10.e: She mounted up, she came to men. They called her, Come unto- us, come hither thou Free-giver! Earth was her milking-pail, the calf beside her Manu Vaivasvata, Vivasvān's offspring. Prithi the son of Vena was her milker: he milked forth hus- bandry and grain for sowing. These men depend for life on corn and tillage. He who knows this becomes a meet supporter, successful in the culture of his_ corn-land.

8.10.d: सो॒द् अक्रामत् सा॒ सप्तऋषी॒न् आ॒गछत् तां॒ सप्तऋष॒य उ॒पाह्वयन्त ब्र॒ह्मण्वत्य् ए॒ही॒ति । त॒स्याः सो॒मो रा॒जा वत्स॒ आ॒सीच् छ॒न्दः पा॒त्रम् । तां॒ बृ॒हस्प॒तिर् आङ्गिरसो॒ ऽधोक् तां॒ ब्र॒ह्म च त॒पश् चाधोक् । त॒द् ब्र॒ह्म च त॒पश् च सप्तऋष॒य उ॒प जीवन्ति ब्रह्मवर्चस्य् उ॑पजीवनी॒यो भवति य॒ एवं॒ वे॒द ॥२५॥ {२८}
8.10.e: She rose, she came unto the Seven Rishis. They called her,. Come, Rich in Devotion! hither. King Soma was her calf. the Moon her milk-pail. Brihaspati. Āngirasa, her milker, Drew from her udder Prayer and Holy Fervour. Fervour and Prayer maintain the Seven Rishis. He who knows this becomes a meet supporter, a priest illustri- ous for his sacred knowledge.

8.10.d: सो॒द् अक्रामत् सा॒ देवा॒न् आ॒गछत् तां॒ देवा॒ उ॒पाह्वयन्तो॒र्ज ए॒ही॒ति । त॒स्या इ॒न्द्रो वत्स॒ आ॒सीच् चमसः॒ पा॒त्रम् । तां॒ देवः॒ सविता॒धोक् ता॒म् ऊर्जा॒म् एवा॒धोक् । तां॒ ऊर्जां॒ देवा॒ उ॒प जीवन्त्य् उपजीवनी॒यो भवति य॒ एवं॒ वे॒द ॥२६॥
8.10.e: She rose, she came unto the Gods. They called her, crying, O Vigour, come to us, come hither! God Savitar milked her, he milked forth Vigour. The Gods depend for life upon that Vigour. He who knows this becomes a meet supporter.

8.10.d: सो॒द् अक्रामत् सा॒ गन्धर्वाप्सर॒स आ॒गछत् तां॒ गन्धर्वाप्सर॒स उ॒पाह्वयन्त पु॒ण्यगन्ध ए॒ही॒ति । त॒स्याश् चित्र॒रथः सौर्यवर्चसो॒ वत्स॒ आ॒सीत् पुष्करपर्णं॒ पा॒त्रम् । तां॒ व॒सुरुचिः सौर्यवर्चसो॒ ऽधोक् तां॒ पु॒ण्यम् एव॒ गन्ध॒म् अधोक् । तं॒ पु॒ण्यं गन्धं॒ गन्धर्वाप्सर॒स उ॒प जीवन्ति पु॒ण्यगन्धिर् उपजीवनी॒यो भवति य॒ एवं॒ वे॒द ॥२७॥
8.10.e: She rose approached the Apsarases and Gandharvas. They called her, Come to us, O Fragrant-scented! The son of Sūryavarchas, Chitraratha, was her dear calf, her pail. a lotus-petal. The son of Sūryavarchas, Vasuruchi, milked and drew from her most delightful fragrance. That scent supports Apsarases and Gandharvas. He who knows this becomes a meet supporter, and round him ever breathes delicious odour.

8.10.d: सो॒द् अक्रामत् से॒तरजना॒न् आ॒गछत् ता॒म् इतरजना॒ उ॒पाह्वयन्त ति॒रोध ए॒ही॒ति । त॒स्याः कु॒बेरो वैश्रवणो॒ वत्स॒ आ॒सीद् आमपात्रं॒ पा॒त्रम् । तां॒ रजत॒नाभिः कबेरको॒ ऽधोक् तां॒ तिरोधा॒म् एवा॒धोक् । तां॒ तिरोधा॒म् अतिरजना॒ पित॒र उ॒प जीवन्ति तिरो॒ धत्ते
8.10.e: She mounted up, she came to Other People. They called her, crying, Come, Concealment! hither. Her dear calf was Vaisravana Kubera, a vessel never tempered was her milk-pail. Rajatanābhi, offspring of Kubera, milked her, and from her udder drew concealment. By that concealment live the Other People. He who knows this becomes a meet supporter, and makes all evil disappear and vanish.

8.10.d: सो॒द् अक्रामत् सा॒ सर्पा॒न् आ॒गछत् तां॒ सर्पा॒ उ॒पाह्वयन्त वि॒षवत्य् ए॒ही॒ति । त॒स्यास् तक्षको॒ वैशलेयो॒ वत्स॒ आ॒सीद् अलाबुपात्रं॒ पा॒त्रं । तां॒ धृत॒राष्ट्र ऐरावतो॒ ऽधोक् तां॒ विष॒म् एवा॒धोक् । त॒द् विषं॒ सर्वा॒ उ॒प जीवन्त्य् उपजीवनी॒यो भवति य॒ एवं॒ वे॒द ॥२९॥ {२९}
8.10.e: She mounted up, she came unto the Serpents. The Serpents called her, Venomous! come hither. Her calf was Takshaka, Visāla's offspring: a bottlegourd suppli- ed a milking-vessel. Irāvān's offspring, Dhritarāshtra milked her, and from her udder drew forth only poison. That poison quickens and supports the Serpents: He who knows this becomes a meet supporter.

8.10.d: त॒द् य॒स्मा एवं॒ विदु॒षे ऽला॒बुनाभिषिञ्चे॒त् प्रत्या॒हन्यात् ॥३०॥
8.10.e: One would ward off, for him who hath this knowledge, if with a bottle-gourd he sprinkled water.

8.10.d: न॒ च प्रत्याहन्या॒न् म॒नसा त्वा॒ प्रत्या॒हन्मी॒ति प्रत्या॒हन्यात् ॥३१॥
8.10.e: And did he not repel, if in his spirit he said, I drive thee back, he would repel it.

8.10.d: य॒त् प्रत्याह॒न्ति विष॒म् एव॒ त॒त् प्रत्या॒हन्ति ॥३२॥
8.10.e: The poison that it drives away, that poison verily repels.

8.10.d: विष॒म् एवा॒स्या॒प्रियं भ्रा॒तृव्यम् अनुवि॒षिच्यते य॒ एवं॒ वे॒द ॥३३॥ {३०}
8.10.e: The man who hath this knowledge pours its venom on his hated foe.

9.1.d: दिव॒स् पृथिव्या॒ अन्त॒रिक्षात् समुद्रा॒द् अग्ने॒र् वा॒तान् मधुकशा॒ हि॒ जज्ञे॒ । तां॒ चायित्वा॒मृ॒तं व॒सानां हृद्भिः॒ प्रजाः॒ प्र॒ति नन्दन्ति स॒र्वाः ॥१॥
9.1.e: The Asvins' Honey-whip was born from heaven and earth, from middle air, and ocean, and from fire and wind. All living creatures welcome it with joyful hearts, fraught with the store of Amrit it hath gathered up.

9.1.d: मह॒त् प॒यो विश्व॒रूपम् अस्याः समुद्र॒स्य त्वोत॒ रे॒त आहुः । य॒त ऐ॒ति मधुकशा॒ र॒राणा त॒त् प्राण॒स् त॒द् अमृ॒तं नि॒विष्टम् ॥२॥
9.1.e: They call thee earth's great strength in every form, they call thee too the ocean's genial seed. Whence comes the Honey-whip bestowing bounty, there Vital Spirit is, and Amrit treasured.

9.1.d: प॒श्यन्त्य् अस्याश् चरितं॒ पृथिव्यां॒ पृ॒थङ् न॒रो बहुधा॒ मी॒मांसमानाः । अग्ने॒र् वा॒तान् मधुकशा॒ हि॒ जज्ञे॒ मरु॒ताम् उग्रा॒ नप्तिः॒ ॥३॥
9.1.e: In sundry spots, repeatedly reflecting, men view upon the earth: her course and action; For she, the first-born daughter of the Maruts, derives her origin from Wind and Agni.

9.1.d: माता॒दित्या॒नां दुहिता॒ व॒सूनां प्राणः॒ प्रजा॒नाम् अमृ॒तस्य ना॒भिः । हि॒रण्यवर्णा मधुकशा॒ घृता॒ची महा॒न् भ॒र्गश् चरति म॒र्त्येषु ॥४॥
9.1.e: Daughter of Vasus, mother of Ādityas, centre of Amrit breath of living creatures. The Honey-whip, gold-coloured, dropping fatness, moves as a mighty embryo 'mid mortals.

9.1.d: म॒धोः क॒शाम् अजनयन्त देवा॒स् त॒स्या ग॒र्भो अभवद् विश्व॒रूपः । तं॒ जातं॒ त॒रुणं पिपर्ति माता॒ स॒ जातो॒ वि॒श्वा भु॒वना वि॒ चष्टे ॥५॥
9.1.e: The deities begat the Whip of Honey: her embryo assumed all forms and fashions. The mother nourishes that tender infant which at its birth looks on all worlds and beings.

9.1.d: क॒स् तं॒ प्र॒ वेद क॒ उ तं॒ चिकेत यो॒ अस्या हृदः॒ कल॒शः सोमधा॒नो अ॒क्षितः । ब्रह्मा॒ सुमेधाः॒ सो॒ अस्मिन् मदेत ॥६॥
9.1.e: Who understandeth well, who hath perceived it, her heart's un- injured Soma-holding beaker? Let the wise Brāhman priest therein be joyful.

9.1.d: स॒ तौ॒ प्र॒ वेद स॒ उ तौ॒ चिकेत या॒व् अस्याः स्त॒नौ सह॒स्रधाराव् अ॒क्षितौ । ऊ॒र्जं दुहाते अ॒नपस्फुरन्तौ ॥७॥
9.1.e: He understandeth them, he hath perceived them, her breasts that pour a thousand streams, uninjured. They unreluctantly yield strength and vigour.

9.1.d: हिङ्क॒रिक्रती बृहती॒ वयोधा॒ उच्चै॒र्घोषाभ्ये॒ति या॒ व्रत॒म् । त्री॒न् घर्मा॒न् अभि॒ वावशाना॒ मि॒माति मायुं॒ प॒यते प॒योभिः ॥८॥
9.1.e: She who with voice upraised in constant clamour, mighty, life- giving, goes unto her function, Bellowing to the heated three libations, suckles with streams of milk, and still is lowing.

9.1.d: या॒म् आ॒पीनाम् उपसी॒दन्त्य् आ॒पः शाक्वरा॒ वृषभा॒ ये॒ स्वरा॒जः । ते॒ वर्षन्ति ते॒ वर्षयन्ति तद्वि॒दे का॒मम् ऊ॒र्जम् आ॒पः ॥९॥
9.1.e: On whom, well-fed, the Waters wait in worship, and steers and self-refulgent bulls attend her. For thee, for one like thee down pour the Waters, and cause desire and strength to rain upon thee.

9.1.d: स्तनयित्नु॒स् ते वा॒क् प्रजापते वृ॒षा शु॒ष्मं क्षिपसि भू॒म्याम् अ॒धि । अग्ने॒र् वा॒तान् मधुकशा॒ हि॒ जज्ञे॒ मरु॒ताम् उग्रा॒ नप्तिः॒ ॥१०॥ {१}
9.1.e: The thunder is thy voice, O Lord of Creatures: a Bull, thou castest on the earth thy vigour. The Honey-whip, the Manus' first-born daughter, derives her origin from Wind and Agni.

9.1.d: य॒था सो॒मः प्रातःसवने॒ अश्वि॒नोर् भवति प्रियः॒ । एवा॒ मे अश्विना व॒र्च आत्म॒नि ध्रियताम् ॥११॥
9.1.e: As at the morning sacrifice the Asvins twain love Soma well, Even so may both the Asvins lay splendour and strength within my soul.

9.1.d: य॒था सो॒मो द्विती॒ये स॒वन इन्द्राग्न्यो॒र् भवति प्रियः॒ । एवा॒ म इन्द्राग्नी व॒र्च आत्म॒नि ध्रियताम् ॥१२॥
9.1.e: As at the second sacrifice Indra and Agni love him well, Let the pair, Indra Agni, lay splendour and strength within my soul.

9.1.d: य॒था सो॒मस् तृती॒ये स॒वन ऋभूणां॒ भवति प्रियः॒ । एवा॒ म ऋभवो व॒र्च आत्म॒नि ध्रियताम् ॥१३॥
9.1.e: As at third sacrifice Soma is the Ribhus' well-beloved one, Even so may they, the Ribhus, store splendour and strength within my soul.

9.1.d: म॒धु जनिषीय म॒धु वंसिषीय । प॒यस्वान् अग्न आ॒गमं तं॒ मा सं॒ सृज व॒र्चसा ॥१४॥
9.1.e: Fain would I bring forth sweetness, fain would make it mine. Bringing milk, Agni! have I come: splendour and strength bestow on me!

9.1.d: सं॒ माग्ने व॒र्चसा सृज सं॒ प्रज॒या स॒म् आ॒युषा । विद्यु॒र् मे अस्य॒ देवा॒ इ॒न्द्रो विद्यात् सह॒ ऋ॒षिभिः ॥१५॥
9.1.e: Grant me, O Agni, splendid strength, and progeny, and length- ened life. May the Gods know me as I am, may Indra with the Rishis know.

9.1.d: य॒था म॒धु मधुकृ॒तः संभ॒रन्ति म॒धाव् अ॒धि । एवा॒ मे अश्विना व॒र्च आत्म॒नि ध्रियताम् ॥१६॥
9.1.e: As honey-bees collect and add fresh honey to their honey store, Even so may both the Asvins lay splendour and strength within my soul.

9.1.d: य॒था म॒क्षाः इदं॒ म॒धु न्यञ्ज॒न्ति म॒धाव् अ॒धि । एवा॒ मे अश्विना व॒र्चस् ते॒जो ब॒लम् ओ॒जश् च ध्रियताम् ॥१७॥
9.1.e: As over honey flies besmear this honey which the bees have made, So may both Asvins lay in me splendour and strength and power and might.

9.1.d: य॒द् गिरि॒षु प॒र्वतेषु गो॒ष्व् अ॒श्वेषु य॒न् म॒धु । सु॒रायां सिच्य॒मानायां य॒त् त॒त्र म॒धु त॒न् म॒यि ॥१८॥
9.1.e: May all the sweetness that is found in hills and mountains, steeds and kine, And wine that floweth from the cup,—may all that sweetness be in me.

9.1.d: अ॒श्विना सारघे॒ण मा म॒धुनाङ्क्तं शुभस् पती । य॒था व॒र्चस्वतीं वा॒चम् आव॒दानि ज॒नां अ॒नु ॥१९॥
9.1.e: May both the Asvins, Lords of Light, balm me with honey of the bees, That I may speak among the folk words full of splendour and of strength.

9.1.d: स्तनयित्नु॒स् ते वा॒क् प्रजापते वृ॒षा शु॒ष्मं क्षिपसि भू॒म्यां दिवि॒ । तां॒ पश॒व उ॒प जीवन्ति स॒र्वे ते॒नो से॒षम् ऊ॒र्जं पिपर्ति ॥२०॥
9.1.e: The thunder is thy voice, O Lord of Creatures: a Bull, thou castest strength on earth and heaven. To that all cattle look for their existence: with this she nourishes their force and vigour.

9.1.d: पृथिवी॒ दण्डो॒ ऽन्त॒रिक्षं ग॒र्भो द्यौः॒ क॒शा विद्यु॒त् प्रकशो॒ हिरण्य॒यो बिन्दुः॒ ॥२१॥
9.1.e: The Whip itself is Heaven, Earth is the handle, the point of juncture is the Air's mid-region. The lash is lightning, and the tip is golden.

9.1.d: यो॒ वै॒ क॒शायाः सप्त॒ म॒धूनि वे॒द म॒धुमान् भवति । ब्राह्मण॒श् च रा॒जा च धेनु॒श् चानड्वां॒श् च व्रीहि॒श् च य॒वश् च म॒धु सप्तम॒म् ॥२२॥
9.1.e: Whoever knows the Whip's seven kinds of honey, becomes himself a man endowed with sweetness. Brāhman and King, the draught-ox and the milch-cow, barley and rice, and honey is the seventh.

9.1.d: म॒धुमान् भवति म॒धुमद् अस्याहार्यं॑ भवति । म॒धुमतो लोका॒न् जयति य॒ एवं॒ वे॒द ॥२३॥
9.1.e: Sweet is the man, sweet are his goods and chattels: he who knows this conquers the worlds of sweetness.

9.1.d: य॒द् वीध्रे॒ स्तन॒यति प्रजा॒पतिर् एव॒ त॒त् प्रजा॒भ्यः प्रादु॒र् भवति । त॒स्मात् प्राचीनोपवीत॒स् तिष्ठे प्र॒जापते॒ ऽनु मा बुध्यस्वे॒ति । अ॒न्व् एनं प्रजा॒ अ॒नु प्रजा॒पतिर् बुध्यते य॒ एवं॒ वे॒द ॥२४॥ {२}
9.1.e: The thundering of Prajāpati in heaven is verily manifest to living creatures. Therefore I stand from right to left invested, and, O Prajāpati, I cry, regard me! The man who hath this knowledge is regarded by living beings and the Lord of Creatures.

9.2.d: सपत्नह॒नम् ऋषभं॒ घृते॒न का॒मं शिक्षामि हवि॒षा॒ज्येन । नीचैः॒ सप॒त्नान् म॒म पदय त्व॒म् अभि॒ष्टुतो महता॒ वीर्ये॑ण ॥१॥
9.2.e: Kāma the Bull, slayer of foes, I worship with molten butter, sacrifice, oblation. Beneath my feet cast down mine adversaries with thy great manly power, when I have praised thee.

9.2.d: य॒न् मे म॒नसो न॒ प्रियं॒ च॒क्षुषो य॒न् मे ब॒भस्ति ना॒भिन॒न्दति । त॒द् दुष्व॒प्न्यं प्र॒ति मुञ्चामि सप॒त्ने का॒मं स्तुत्वो॒द् अहं॒ भिदेयम् ॥२॥
9.2.e: That which is hateful to mine eye and spirit, that harasses and robs me of enjoyment, The evil dream I loose upon my foemen. May I rend him when I have lauded Kāma.

9.2.d: दुष्व॒प्न्यं काम दुरितं॒ च कमाप्रज॒स्ताम् अस्वग॒ताम् अ॒वर्तिम् । उग्र॒ ई॒शानः प्र॒ति मुञ्च त॒स्मिन् यो॒ अस्म॒भ्यम् अंहूरणा॒ चि॒कित्सात् ॥३॥
9.2.e: Kāma, do thou, a mighty Lord and Ruler, let loose ill dream, misfortune, want of children, Homelessness, Kāma! utter destitution, upon the sinner who designs my ruin.

9.2.d: नुद॒स्व काम प्र॒ णुदस्व कामा॒वर्तिं यन्तु म॒म ये॒ सप॒त्नाः । ते॒षां नुत्ता॒नाम् अधमा॒ त॒मांस्य् अ॒ग्ने वा॒स्तूनि नि॒र् दह त्व॒म् ॥४॥
9.2.e: Drive them away, drive them afar, O Kāma; indigence fall on those who are my foemen! When they have been cast down to deepest darkness, consume their dwellings with thy fire, O Agni.

9.2.d: सा॒ ते काम दुहिता॒ धेनु॒र् उच्यते या॒म् आहु॒र् वा॒चं कव॒यो विरा॒जम् । त॒या सप॒त्नान् प॒रि वृङ्ग्धि ये॒ म॒म प॒र्य् एनान् प्राणः॒ पश॒वो जी॒वनं वृणक्तु ॥५॥
9.2.e: She, Kāma! she is called the Cow, thy daughter, she who is named Vāk and Virāj by sages. By her drive thou my foemen to a distance. May cattle, vital breath, and life forsake them.

9.2.d: का॒मस्ये॒न्द्रस्य व॒रुणस्य रा॒ज्ञो वि॒ष्णोर् ब॒लेन सवितुः॒ सवे॒न । अग्ने॒र् होत्रे॒ण प्र॒ णुदे सप॒त्नां छम्बी॒व ना॒वम् उदके॒षु धी॒रः ॥६॥
9.2.e: By Kāma's might, King Varuna's and Indra's, by Vishnu's strength, and Savitar's instigation, I chase my foes with sacrifice to Agni, as a deft steersman drives his boat through waters.

9.2.d: अ॒ध्यक्षो वाजी॒ म॒म का॒म उग्रः॒ कृणो॒तु म॒ह्यम् असपत्न॒म् एव॒ । वि॒श्वे देवा॒ म॒म नाथं॒ भवन्तु स॒र्वे देवा॒ ह॒वम् आ॒ यन्तु म इम॒म् ॥७॥
9.2.e: May Kāma, mighty one, my potent warder, give me full free- dom from mine adversaries. May all the Deities be my protection, all Gods come nigh to this mine invocation.

9.2.d: इद॒म् आ॒ज्यं घृत॒वज् जुषाणाः॒ का॒मज्येष्ठा इह॒ मादयध्वम् । कृण्व॒न्तो म॒ह्यम् असपत्न॒म् एव॒ ॥८॥
9.2.e: Accepting this oblation rich with fatness, be joyful here, ye Gods whose chief is Kāma, Giving me freedom from mine adversaries.

9.2.d: इन्द्राग्नी॒ काम सर॒थं हि॒ भूत्वा॒ नीचैः॒ सप॒त्नान् म॒म पादयाथः । ते॒षां पन्ना॒नाम् अधमा॒ त॒मांस्य् अ॒ग्ने वा॒स्तून्य् अनुनि॒र्दह त्व॒म् ॥९॥
9.2.e: Ye, Indra, Agni, Kāma! come together and cast mine adver- saries down beneath me. When they have sunk into the deepest darkness, O Agni, with thy fire consume their dwellings.

9.2.d: जहि॒ त्व॒म् काम म॒म ये॒ सप॒त्ना अन्धा॒ त॒मांस्य् अ॒व पादयैनान् । नि॒रिन्द्रिया अरसाः॒ सन्तु स॒र्वे मा॒ ते॒ जीविषुः कतम॒च् चना॒हः ॥१०॥ {३}
9.2.e: Slay those who are mine enemies, O Kāma: headlong to depth of blinding darkness hurl them. Reft be they all of manly strength and vigour! Let them not have a single day's existence.

9.2.d: अ॒वधीत् का॒मो म॒म ये॒ सप॒त्ना उरुं॒ लोक॒म् अकरन् म॒ह्यम् एधतु॒म् । म॒ह्यं नमन्तां प्रदि॒शश् च॒तस्रो म॒ह्यं ष॒ड् उर्वी॒र् घृत॒म् आ॒ वहन्तु ॥११॥
9.2.e: Kāma hath slain those who were mine opponents, and given me ample room to grow and prosper. Let the four regions bow them down before me, and let the six expanses bring me fatness.

9.2.d: ते॒ ऽधरा॒ञ्चः प्र॒ प्लवन्तां छिन्ना॒ नौ॒र् इव ब॒न्धनात् । न॒ सा॒यकप्रणुत्तानां पु॒नर् अस्ति निव॒र्तनम् ॥१२॥
9.2.e: Let them drift downward like a boat torn from the rope that held it fast. There is no turning back for those whom our keen arrows have repelled.

9.2.d: अग्नि॒र् य॒व इ॒न्द्रो य॒वः सो॒मो य॒वः । यवया॒वानो देवा॒ यवयन्त्व् एनम् ॥१३॥
9.2.e: Agni averts, Indra averts, and Soma: may the averting Gods avert this foeman.

9.2.d: अ॒सर्ववीरश् चरतु प्र॒णुत्तो द्वे॒ष्यो मित्रा॒नां परिवर्ग्यः॑ स्वा॒नाम् । उत॒ पृथिव्या॒म् अ॒व स्यन्ति विद्यु॒त उग्रो॒ वो देवः॒ प्र॒ मृणत् सप॒त्नान् ॥१४॥
9.2.e: To be avoided by his friends, detested, repelled, with few men round him, let him wander. Yea, on the earth descend the lightning-flashes: may the strong God destroy your adversaries.

9.2.d: च्युता॒ चेयं॒ बृहत्य् अ॒च्युता च विद्यु॒द् बिभर्ति स्तनयित्नूं॒श् च स॒र्वान् । उद्य॒न्न् आदित्यो॒ द्र॒विणेन ते॒जसा नीचैः॒ सप॒त्नान् नुदतां मे स॒हस्वान् ॥१५॥
9.2.e: This potent lightning nourishes things shaken, and things un- shaken yet, and all the thunders. May the Sun, rising with his wealth and splendour, drive in victorious might my foemen downward.

9.2.d: य॒त् ते काम श॒र्म त्रिव॒रूथम् उद्भु॒ ब्र॒ह्म व॒र्म वि॒ततम् अनतिव्याध्यं॑ कृत॒म् । ते॒न सप॒त्नान् प॒रि वृङ्ग्धि ये॒ म॒म प॒र्य् एनान् प्राणः॒ पश॒वो जी॒वनं वृणक्तु ॥१६॥
9.2.e: Thy firm and triply-barred protection, Kāma! thy spell, made weapon-proof extended armour With that drive thou my foemen to a distance. May cattle, vital breath, and life forsake them.

9.2.d: ये॒न देवा॒ अ॒सुरान् प्रा॒णुदन्त ये॒ने॒न्द्रो द॒स्यून् अधमं॒ त॒मो निना॒य । ते॒न त्वं॒ काम म॒म ये॒ सप॒त्नास् ता॒न् अस्मा॒ल् लोका॒त् प्र॒ णुदस्व दूर॒म् ॥१७॥
9.2.e: Far from the world wherein we live, O Kāma, drive thou my foemen with that selfsame weapon Wherewith the Gods repelled the fiends, and Indra cast down the Dasyus into deepest darkness.

9.2.d: य॒था देवा॒ अ॒सुरान् प्रा॒णुदन्त य॒थे॒न्द्रो द॒स्यून् अधमं॒ त॒मो बबाधे॒ । त॒था त्वं॒ काम म॒म ये॒ सप॒त्नास् ता॒न् अस्मा॒ल् लोका॒त् प्र॒ णुदस्व दूर॒म् ॥१८॥
9.2.e: As Gods repelled the Asuras, and Indra down to the lowest darkness drove the demons, So, Kāma, from this world, to distant places, drive thou the men who are mine adversaries.

9.2.d: का॒मो जज्ञे प्रथमो॒ नै॒नं देवा॒ आपुः पित॒रो न॒ म॒र्त्याः । त॒तस् त्व॒म् असि ज्या॒यान् विश्व॒हा महां॒स् त॒स्मै ते काम न॒म इ॒त् कृनोमि ॥१९॥
9.2.e: First before all sprang Kāma into being. Gods, Fathers, mortal men have never matched him. Stronger than these art thou, and great for ever. Kāma, to thee, to thee I offer worship.

9.2.d: या॒वती द्या॒वापृथिवी॒ वरिम्णा॒ या॒वद् आ॒पः सिष्यदु॒र् या॒वद् अग्निः॒ । त॒तस् त्व॒म् असि ज्या॒यान् विश्व॒हा महां॒स् त॒स्मै ते काम न॒म इ॒त् कृणोमि ॥२०॥ {४}
9.2.e: Wide as the space which heaven and earth encompass, far as the flow of waters, far as Agni, Stronger than these art thou, and great for ever. Kāma, to thee, to thee I offer worship.

9.2.d: या॒वतीर् दि॒शः प्रदि॒शो वि॒षूचीर् या॒वतीर् आ॒शा अभिच॒क्षणा दिवः॒ । त॒तस् त्व॒म् असि ज्या॒यान् विश्व॒हा महां॒स् त॒स्मै ते काम न॒म इ॒त् कृणोमि ॥२१॥
9.2.e: Vast as the quarters of the sky and regions that lie between them spread in all directions, vast as celestial tracts and views of heaven, Stronger than these art thou, and great for ever. Kāma, to thee, to thee I offer worship.

9.2.d: या॒वतीर् भृ॒ङ्गा जत्वः॑ कुरू॒रवो या॒वतीर् व॒घा वृक्षसर्प्यो॑ बभूवुः॒ । त॒तस् त्व॒म् असि ज्या॒यान् विश्व॒हा महां॒स् त॒स्मै ते काम न॒म इ॒त् कृणोमि ॥२२॥
9.2.e: Many as are the bees, and bats, and reptiles, and female serpents of the trees, and beetles, Stronger art thou than these, and great for ever. Kāma, to thee, to thee I offer worship.

9.2.d: ज्या॒यान् निमिषतो॒ ऽसि ति॒ष्ठतो ज्या॒यान्त् समुद्रा॒द् असि काम मन्यो । त॒तस् त्व॒म् असि ज्या॒यान् विश्व॒हा महां॒स् त॒स्मै ते काम न॒म इ॒त् कृनोमि ॥२३॥
9.2.e: Stronger art thou than aught that stands or twinkles, stronger art thou than ocean, Kāma! Manyu! Stronger than these art thou, and great for ever. Kāma, to thee, to thee I offer worship.

9.2.d: न॒ वै॒ वा॒तश् चन॒ का॒मम् आप्नोति ना॒ग्निः॒ सू॒र्यो नो॒त॒ चन्द्र॒माः । त॒तस् त्व॒म् असि ज्या॒यान् विश्व॒हा महां॒स् त॒स्मै ते काम न॒म इ॒त् कृणोमि ॥२४॥
9.2.e: Not even Vāta is the peer of Kāma, not Agni, Chandramas the Moon, nor Sūrya. Stronger than these art thou, and great for ever. Kāma, to thee, to thee I offer worship.

9.2.d: या॒स् ते शिवा॒स् तन्वः॑ काम भद्रा॒ या॒भिः सत्यं॒ भ॒वति य॒द् वृणिषे॒ । ता॒भिष् ट्व॒म् अस्मां॒ अभिसं॒विशस्वान्य॒त्र पापी॒र् अ॒प वेशया धि॒यः ॥२५॥ {५}
9.2.e: Thy lovely and auspicious forms, O Kāma, whereby the thing thou wilt becometh real, With these come thou and make thy home among us, and make malignant thoughts inhabit elsewhere.

9.3.d: उपमि॒तां प्रतिमि॒ताम् अ॒थो परिमि॒ताम् उत॒ । शा॒लाया विश्व॒वाराया नद्धा॒नि वि॒ चृतामसि ॥१॥
9.3.e: We loose the ties and fastenings of the house that holds all precious things, The bands of pillars and of stays, the ties of beams that form the roof.

9.3.d: य॒त् ते नद्धं॒ विश्ववारे पा॒शो ग्रन्थि॒श् च यः॒ कृतः॒ । बृ॒हस्प॒तिर् इवाहं॒ बलं॒ वाचा॒ वि॒ स्रंसयामि त॒त् ॥२॥
9.3.e: All-wealthy House! each knot and band, each cord that is attached to thee I with my spell untie, as erst Brihaspati disclosed the cave.

9.3.d: आ॒ ययाम सं॒ बबर्ह ग्रन्थीं॒श् चकार ते दृढा॒न् । प॒रूंषि विद्वां॒ छ॒स्तेवे॒न्द्रेण वि॒ चृतामसि ॥३॥
9.3.e: He drew them close, he pressed them fast, he made thy knotted. bands secure: With Indra's help we loose them as a skilful Slaughterer severs joints.

9.3.d: वंशा॒नां ते न॒हनानां प्राणाह॒स्य तृ॒णस्य च । पक्षा॒णां विश्ववारे ते नद्धा॒नि वि॒ चृतामसि ॥४॥
9.3.e: We loose the bands of thy bamboos, of bolts, of fastening, of thatch, We loose the ties of thy side-posts, O House that holdest all we prize.

9.3.d: संदंशा॒नां पलदा॒नां प॒रिष्वञ्जल्यस्य च । इदं॒ मा॒नस्य प॒त्न्या नद्धा॒नि वि॒ चृतामसि ॥५॥
9.3.e: We loosen here the ties and bands of straw in bundles, and of clamps, Of all that compasses and binds the Lady Genius of the Home.

9.3.d: या॒नि ते ऽन्तः॒ शिक्या॑न्य् आबेधू॒ रण्या॑य क॒म् । प्र॒ ते ता॒नि चृतामसि शिवा॒ मानस्य पत्नि न उ॒द्धिता तन्वे॑ भव ॥६॥
9.3.e: We loose the loops which men have bound within thee, loops to tie and hold. Be gracious, when erected, to our bodies, Lady of the Home.

9.3.d: हविर्धा॒नम् अग्निशा॒लं प॒त्नीनां स॒दनं स॒दः । स॒दो देवा॒नाम् असि देवि शाले ॥७॥
9.3.e: Store-house of Soma, Agni's hall, the ladies' bower, the resi- dence, The seat of Gods art thou, O Goddess House.

9.3.d: अ॒क्षुम् ओ॒पशं॒ वि॒ततं सहस्राक्षं॒ विषूव॒ति । अ॒वनद्धम् अभि॒हितं ब्र॒ह्मणा वि॒ चृतामसि ॥८॥
9.3.e: We with our incantation loose the net that hath a thousand. eyes. The diadem, securely tied and laid upon the central beam.

9.3.d: य॒स् त्वा शाले प्रतिगृह्णा॒ति ये॒न चा॒सि मिता॒ त्व॒म् । उभौ॒ मानस्य पत्नि तौ॒ जी॒वतां जर॒दष्टी ॥९॥
9.3.e: The man who takes thee as his own, and he who was thy builder,. House! Both these, O Lady of the Home, shall live to long-extended' years.

9.3.d: अमु॒त्रैनम् आ॒ गछताद् दृढा॒ नद्धा॒ प॒रिष्कृता । य॒स्यास् ते विचृता॒मस्य् अ॒ङ्गमङ्गं प॒रुष्परुः ॥१०॥ {६}
9.3.e: There let her come to meet this man. Firm, strongly fastened,. and prepared Art thou whose several limbs and joints we part and loosen one by one.

9.3.d: य॒स् त्वा शाले निमिमा॒य संजभा॒र व॒नस्प॒तीन् । प्रजा॒यै चक्रे त्वा शाले परमेष्ठी॒ प्रजा॒पतिः ॥११॥
9.3.e: He who collected timber for the work and built thee up, O House, Made thee for coming progeny, Prajāpati, the Lord Supreme.

9.3.d: न॒मस् त॒स्मै न॒मो दात्रे॒ शा॒लापतये च कृण्मः । न॒मो ऽग्न॒ये प्रच॒रते पु॒रुषाय च ते न॒मः ॥१२॥
9.3.e: Homage to him! We worship too the giver and the Mansion's lord: Homage to Agni! to the man who serves at holy rites for thee.

9.3.d: गो॒भ्यो अ॒श्वेभ्यो न॒मो य॒च् छा॒लायां विजा॒यते । वि॒जावति प्र॒जावति वि॒ ते पा॒शांश् चृतामसि ॥१३॥
9.3.e: Homage to kine and steeds! to all that shall be born within the house We loose the bonds that fasten thee, mother of multitudes to come!

9.3.d: अग्नि॒म् अन्त॒श् छादयसि पु॒रुषान् पशु॒भिः सह॒ । वि॒जावति प्र॒जावति वि॒ ते पा॒शांश् चृतामसि ॥१४॥
9.3.e: Agni thou shelterest within, and people with domestic beasts. We loose the bonds that fasten thee, mother of multitudes to come!

9.3.d: अन्तरा॒ द्यां॒ च पृथिवीं॒ च य॒द् व्य॒चस् ते॒न शा॒लां प्र॒ति गृह्णामि त इमा॒म् । य॒द् अन्त॒रिक्षं र॒जसो विमा॒नं त॒त् कृण्वे ऽह॒म् उद॒रं शेवधि॒भ्यः । ते॒न शा॒लां प्र॒ति गृह्णामि त॒स्मै ॥१५॥
9.3.e: All space that lies between the earth and heaven, therewith I take this house for thy possession, And all that measures out the air's mid-region I make a hollow to contain thy treasures. Therewith I take the house for his possession.

9.3.d: ऊ॒र्जस्वती प॒यस्वती पृथिव्यां॒ नि॒मिता मिता॒ । विश्वान्नं॒ बि॒भ्रती शाले मा॒ हिंसीः प्रतिगृह्णतः॒ ॥१६॥
9.3.e: Rich in prosperity, rich in milk, founded and built upon the earth, Injure not thy receivers, House who holdest food of every sort!'

9.3.d: तृ॒णैर् आ॒वृता पलदा॒न् व॒साना रा॒त्रीव शा॒ला ज॒गतो निवे॒शनी । मिता॒ पृथिव्यां॒ तिष्ठसि हस्ति॒नीव पद्व॒ती ॥१७॥
9.3.e: Grass-covered, clad with straw, the house, like Night, gives rest to man and beast. Thou standest, built upon the earth, like a she-elephant, borne on feet.

9.3.d: इ॒टस्य ते वि॒ चृताम्य् अ॒पिनद्धम् अपोर्णुव॒न् । व॒रुणेन स॒मुब्जितां मित्रः॒ प्रात॒र् व्य् उ॑ब्जतु ॥१८॥
9.3.e: I loosen and remove from thee thy covering formed by mats of reed. What Varuna hath firmly closed Mitra shall ope at early morn.

9.3.d: ब्र॒ह्मणा शा॒लां नि॒मितां कवि॒भिर् नि॒मितां मिता॒म् । इन्द्राग्नी॒ रक्षतां शा॒लाम् अमृ॒तौ सोम्यं॒ स॒दः ॥१९॥
9.3.e: May Indra, Agni, deathless Gods, protect the house where Soma dwells, House that was founded with the prayer, built and erected by the wise.

9.3.d: कुला॒ये॒ ऽधि कुला॒यं को॒शे को॒शः स॒मुब्जितः । त॒त्र म॒र्तो वि॒ जायते य॒स्माद् वि॒श्वं प्रजा॒यते ॥२०॥ {७}
9.3.e: Nest upon nest hath been imposed, compartment on compart- ment laid: There man shall propagate his kind, and there shall everything born.

9.3.d: या॒ द्वि॒पक्षा च॒तुष्पक्षा ष॒ट्पक्षा या॒ निमीय॒ते । अष्टा॒पक्षां द॒शपक्षां शा॒लां मा॒नस्य प॒त्नीम् अग्नि॒र् ग॒र्भ इवा॒ शये ॥२१॥
9.3.e: Within the house constructed with two side-posts, or with four, or six. Built with eight side-posts, or with ten, lies Agni like a babe unborn.

9.3.d: प्रती॒चीं त्वा प्रतीची॒नः शा॒ले प्रै॒म्य् अ॒हिंसतीम् । अग्नि॒र् ह्य् अ॑न्त॒र् आ॒पश् च ऋत॒स्य प्रथमा॒ द्वाः॒ ॥२२॥
9.3.e: Turned to thee, House! I come to thee, innocent, turned to welcome me: For Fire and Water are within, the first chief door of sacrifice.

9.3.d: इमा॒ आ॒पः प्र॒ भराम्य् अयक्ष्मा॒ यक्ष्मना॒शनीः । गृहा॒न् उ॒प प्र॒ सीदाम्य् अमृ॒तेन सहा॒ग्नि॒ना ॥२३॥
9.3.e: Water that kills Consumption, free from all Consumption, here I bring. With Agni, the immortal one, I enter and possess the house.

9.3.d: मा॒ नः पा॒शं प्र॒ति मुचो गुरु॒र् भारो॒ लघु॒र् भव । वधू॒म् इव त्वा शाले यत्रका॒मं भरामसि ॥२४॥
9.3.e: Lay thou no cord or noose on us: a weighty burthen, still be light! Withersoever be our will, O House, we bear thee like a bride.

9.3.d: प्रा॒च्या दिशः॒ शा॒लाया न॒मो महिम्ने॒ स्वा॒हा देवे॒भ्यः स्वाह्ये॑भ्यः ॥२५॥
9.3.e: Now from the east side of the house to the Great Power be homage paid! Hail to the Gods whose due is Hail!

9.3.d: द॒क्षिणाया दिशः॒ शा॒लाया न॒मो महिम्ने॒ स्वा॒हा देवे॒भ्यः स्वाह्ये॑भ्यः ॥२६॥
9.3.e: Now from the south side of the house, etc.

9.3.d: प्रती॒च्या दिशः॒ शा॒लाया न॒मो महिम्ने॒ स्वा॒हा देवे॒भ्यः स्वाह्ये॑भ्यः ॥२७॥
9.3.e: Now from the west side of the house, etc.

9.3.d: उ॒दीच्या दिशः॒ शा॒लाया न॒मो महिम्ने॒ स्वा॒हा देवे॒भ्यः स्वाह्ये॑भ्यः ॥२८॥
9.3.e: Now from the north side of the house, etc.

9.3.d: ध्रुवा॒या दिशः॒ शा॒लाया न॒मो महिम्ने॒ स्वा॒हा देवे॒भ्यः स्वाह्ये॑भ्यः ॥२९॥
9.3.e: So from the mansion's every side to the Great Power be homage paid! Hail to the Gods whose due is Hail!

9.3.d: ऊर्ध्वा॒या दिशः॒ शा॒लाया न॒मो महिम्ने॒ स्वा॒हा देवे॒भ्यः स्वाह्ये॑भ्यः ॥३०॥
दिशो॒दिशः शा॒लाया न॒मो महिम्ने॒ स्वा॒हा देवे॒भ्यः स्वाह्ये॑भ्यः ॥३१॥ {८}

9.4.d: साहस्र॒स् त्वेष॒ ऋषभः॒ प॒यस्वान् वि॒श्वा रूपा॒णि वक्ष॒णासु बि॒भ्रत् । भद्रं॒ दात्रे॒ य॒जमानाय शीक्षन् बार्हस्पत्य॒ उस्रि॒यस् त॒न्तुम् आ॒तान् ॥१॥
9.4.e: The Bull, fierce, thousandfold, filled full of vigour, bearing within his flanks all forms and natures, Brihaspati's Steer, hath stretched the thread, bestowing bliss on the worshipper, the liberal giver.

9.4.d: अपां॒ यो॒ अ॒ग्ने प्रतिमा॒ बभू॒व प्रभूः॒ स॒र्वस्मै पृथिवी॒व देवी॒ । पिता॒ वत्सा॒नां प॒तिर् अघ्न्या॒नां साहस्रे॒ पो॒षे अ॒पि नः कृणोतु ॥२॥
9.4.e: He who at first became the Waters' model, a match for everyone, like Earth the Goddess; The husband of the cows, the young calves' father, may be secure us thousandfold abundance.

9.4.d: पु॒मान् अन्त॒र्वान्त् स्थ॒विरः प॒यस्वान् व॒सोः क॒बन्धं ऋषभो॒ बिभर्ति । त॒म् इ॒न्द्राय पथि॒भिर् देवया॒नैर् हुत॒म् अग्नि॒र् वहतु जात॒वेदाः ॥३॥
9.4.e: Masculine, prégnant, stedfast. full of vigour, the Bull sustains a trunk of goodly treasure. May Agni Jātavedas bear him offered, on pathways traversed by the Gods, to Indra.

9.4.d: पिता॒ वत्सा॒नां प॒तिर् अघ्न्या॒नां अ॒थो पिता॒ महतां॒ ग॒र्गराणाम् । वत्सो॒ जरा॒यु प्रतिधु॒क् पीयू॒ष आमि॒क्षा घृतं॒ त॒द् व् अस्य रे॒तः ॥४॥
9.4.e: The husband of the cows, the young calves' father, father is he of mighty water-eddies. Calf, after-birth, new milk drawn hot, and biestings, curds, butter, that is his best genial humour.

9.4.d: देवा॒नां भाग॒ उपनाह॒ एषो॒ ऽपां॒ र॒स ओ॒षधीनां घृत॒स्य । सो॒मस्य भक्ष॒म् अवृणीत शक्रो॒ बृह॒न्न् अ॒द्रिर् अभवद् य॒च् छ॒रीरम् ॥५॥
9.4.e: He is the Gods' allotted share and bundle, essence of waters, and of plants, and butter. Sakra elected him, the draught of Soma. What was his body was a lofty mountain.

9.4.d: सो॒मेन पूर्णं॒ कल॒शं बिभर्षि त्व॒स्ता रुपा॒णां जनिता॒ पशूना॒म् । शिवा॒स् ते सन्तु प्रजन्व॑ इह॒ या॒ इमा॒ न्य् अ॑स्म॒भ्यं स्वधिते यछ या॒ अमूः॒ ॥६॥
9.4.e: A beaker filled with Soma juice thou bearest. framer of forms, begetter of the cattle. Kindly to us be these thy wombs here present, and stay for us, O Axe, those that are yonder.

9.4.d: आ॒जं बिभर्ति घृत॒म् अस्य रे॒तः साहस्रः॒ पो॒षस् त॒म् उ यज्ञ॒म् आहुः । इ॒न्द्रस्य रूप॒म् ऋषभो॒ व॒सानः सो॒ अस्मा॒न् देवाः शिव॒ ऐ॒तु दत्तः॒ ॥७॥
9.4.e: He bears oblation, and his seed is butter. Thousand-fold plenty; sacrifice they call him. May he, the Bull, wearing the shape of Indra, come unto us, O Gods, bestowed, with blessing.

9.4.d: इ॒न्द्रस्यौ॒जो व॒रुणस्य बाहू॒ अश्वि॒नोर् अं॒सौ मरु॒ताम् इयं॒ ककु॒त् । बृ॒हस्प॒तिं सं॒भृतम् एत॒म् आहुर् ये॒ धी॒रासः कव॒यो ये॒ मनीषि॒णः ॥८॥
9.4.e: Both arms of Varuna, and Indra's vigour, the Maruts' hump is he, the Asvins' shoulders. They who are sages, bards endowed with wisdom, call him Brihaspati compact and heightened.

9.4.d: दै॒वीर् वि॒शः प॒यस्वान् आ॒ तनोषि त्वा॒म् इ॒न्द्रं त्वां॒ स॒रस्वन्तम् आहुः । सह॒स्रं स॒ ए॒कमुखा ददाति यो॒ ब्राह्मण॒ ऋषभ॒म् आजुहो॒ति ॥९॥
9.4.e: Thou, vigorous, reachest to the tribes of heaven. Thee they call Indra, thee they call Sarasvān. Turned to one aim, that Brāhman gives a thousand who offers up the Bull as his oblation.

9.4.d: बृ॒हस्प॒तिः सविता॒ ते व॒यो दधौ त्व॒ष्टुर् वायोः॒ प॒र्य् आत्मा॒ त आ॒भृतः । अन्त॒रिक्षे म॒नसा त्वा जुहोमि बर्हि॒ष् टे द्या॒वापृथिवी॒ उभे॒ स्ताम् ॥१०॥ {९}
9.4.e: Brihaspati, Savitar gave thee vital vigour: thy breath was brought from Tvashtar and from Vāyu. In thought I offer thee in air's mid-region. Thy sacrificial grass be Earth and Heaven!

9.4.d: य॒ इ॒न्द्र इव देवे॒षु गो॒ष्व् एति विवा॒वदत् । त॒स्य ऋषभ॒स्या॒ङ्गानि ब्रह्मा॒ सं॒ स्तौतु भद्र॒या ॥११॥
9.4.e: Let the priest joyfully extol the limbs and members of the Bull Who moved and roared among the kine as Indra moves among the Gods.

9.4.d: पार्श्वे॒ आस्ताम् अ॒नुमत्या भ॒गस्यास्ताम् अनूवृ॒जौ । अष्ठीव॒न्ताव् अब्रवीन् मित्रो॒ म॒मैतौ॒ के॒वलाव् इ॒ति ॥१२॥
9.4.e: The sides must be Anumati's, and both rib-pieces Bhaga's share, Of the knee-bones hath Mitra said, Both these are mine, and only mine.

9.4.d: भस॒द् आसीद् आदित्या॒नां श्रो॒णी आस्तां बृ॒हस्प॒तेः । पु॒छं वा॒तस्य देव॒स्य ते॒न धूनोत्य् ओ॒षधीः ॥१३॥
9.4.e: The Ādityas claim the hinder parts, the loins must be Brihas- pati's. Vāta, the God, receives the tail: he stirs the plants and herbs therewith,

9.4.d: गु॒दा आसन्त् सिनीवाल्याः॒ सूर्या॒यास् त्व॒चम् अब्रुवन् । उत्थातु॒र् अब्रुवन् पद॒ ऋषभं॒ य॒द् अ॒कल्पयन् ॥१४॥
9.4.e: To Sūryā they assigned the skin, to Sinivāli inward parts. The Slaughterer hath the feet, they said, when they distributed the Bull.

9.4.d: क्रोड॒ आसीज् जामिशंस॒स्य सो॒मस्य क्ल॒शो धृतः॒ । देवाः॒ संग॒त्य य॒त् स॒र्व ऋषभं॒ व्य॒कल्पयन् ॥१५॥
9.4.e: They made a jest of kindred's curse: a jar of Soma juice was set, What time the deities, convened, assigned the Bull's divided parts.

9.4.d: ते॒ कु॒ष्ठिकाः सर॒मायै कुर्मे॒भ्यो अदधुः शफा॒न् । ऊ॒बध्यम् अस्य कीते॒भ्यः श्ववर्ते॒भ्यो अधारयन् ॥१६॥
9.4.e: They gave the hooves to tortoises, to Saramā scraps of the feet: His undigested food they gave to worms and things that creep and crawl.

9.4.d: शृ॒ङ्गाभ्यां र॒क्ष ऋषत्य् अ॒वर्तिम् हन्ति च॒क्षुषा । शृणो॒ति भद्रं॒ क॒र्णाभ्यां ग॒वां यः॒ प॒तिर् अघ्न्यः॒ ॥१७॥
9.4.e: That Bull, the husband of the kine, pierces the demons with his horns, Banishes famine with his eye, and hears good tidings with his ears.

9.4.d: शतया॒जं स॒ यजते नै॒नं दुन्वन्त्य् अग्न॒यः । जि॒न्वन्ति वि॒श्वे तं॒ देवा॒ यो॒ ब्राह्मण॒ ऋषभ॒म् आजुहो॒ति ॥१८॥
9.4.e: With hundred sacrifices he worships: the fires consume him not: All Gods promote the Braman who offers the Bull in sacrifice.

9.4.d: ब्राह्मणे॒भ्य ऋषभं॒ दत्त्वा॒ व॒रीयः कृणुते म॒नः । पु॒ष्टिं सो॒ अघ्न्या॒नां स्वे॒ गोष्ठे॒ ऽव पश्यते ॥१९॥
9.4.e: He who hath given away the Bull to Brāhmans frees and cheers his soul. In his own cattle-pen he sees the growth and increase of his cows.

9.4.d: गा॒वः सन्तु प्रजाः॒ सन्त्व् अ॒थो अस्तु तनूबल॒म् । त॒त् स॒र्वम् अ॒नु मन्यन्तां देवा॒ ऋषभदायि॒ने ॥२०॥
9.4.e: Let there be cattle, let there be bodily strength and progeny: All this may the Gods kindly grant to him who gives away the Bull.

9.4.d: अयं॒ पिपान इ॒न्द्र इ॒द् रयिं॒ दधातु चेतनी॒म् । अयं॒ धेनुं॒ सुदु॒घां नि॒त्यवत्सां व॒शं दुहां विपश्चि॒तं परो॒ दिवः॒ ॥२१॥
9.4.e: Indra here verily hath rejoiced: let him bestow conspicuous wealth. May he draw forth at will from yonder side of heaven a deft cow, good to milk, whose calf is never wanting.

9.4.d: पिश॒ङ्गरूपो नभसो॒ वयोधा॒ ऐन्द्रः॒ शु॒ष्मो विश्व॒रूपो न आ॒गन् । आ॒युर् अस्म॒भ्यं द॒धत् प्रजां॒ च राय॒श् च पो॒षैर् अभि॒ नः सचताम् ॥२२॥
9.4.e: With close connexion mingle with the cows in this our cattle- pen: Mingle, the Bull's prolific flow, and, Indra! thine heroic strength!

9.4.d: उ॒पेहो॒पपर्चनास्मि॒न् गोष्ठ॒ उ॒प पृञ्च नः । उ॒प ऋषभ॒स्य य॒द् रे॒त उ॒पेन्द्र त॒व वीर्य॑म् ॥२३॥
9.4.e: Here we restore this Bull, your youthful leader: sporting with him, go, wander at your pleasure. Ne'er, wealthy ones! may he be reft of offspring; and do ye favour us with growth of riches.

9.4.d: एतं॒ वो यु॒वानं प्र॒ति दध्मो अ॒त्र ते॒न क्री॒डन्तीश् चरत व॒शां अ॒नु । मा॒ नो हासिष्ट जनु॒षा सुभागा राय॒श् च पो॒षैर् अभि॒ नः सचध्वम् ॥२४॥ {१०}

9.5.d: आ॒ नयैत॒म् आ॒ रभस्व सुकृ॒तां लोक॒म् अ॒पि गछतु प्रजान॒न् । तीर्त्वा॒ त॒मांसि बहुधा॒ महा॒न्त्य् अजो॒ ना॒कम् आ॒ क्रमतां तृती॒यम् ॥१॥
9.5.e: Seize him and bring him hither. Let him travel. foreknowing, to the regions of the pious. Crossing in many a place the mighty darkness, let the Goat mount to the third heaven above us.

9.5.d: इ॒न्द्राय भागं॒ प॒रि त्वा नयाम्य् अस्मि॒न् यज्ञे॒ य॒जमानाय सूरि॒म् । ये॒ नो द्विष॒न्त्य् अ॒नु ता॒न् रभस्वा॒नागसो य॒जमानस्य वीराः॒ ॥२॥
9.5.e: I bring thee hither as a share for Indra; prince, at this sacrifice,. for him who worships. Grasp firmly from behind all those who hate us: so let the sacri- ficer's men be sinless.

9.5.d: प्र॒ पदो॒ ऽव नेनिग्धि दु॒श्चरितं य॒च् चचा॒र शुद्धैः॒ शफै॒र् आ॒ क्रमतां प्रजान॒न् । तीर्त्वा॒ त॒मांसि बहुधा॒ विप॒श्यन्न् अजो॒ ना॒कम् आ॒ क्रमतां तृती॒यम् ॥३॥
9.5.e: Wash from his feet all trace of evil-doing: foreknowing, with cleansed hooves let him go upward. Gazing on many a spot, crossing the darkness, let the Goat mount to the third heaven above us.

9.5.d: अ॒नुछ्य श्यामे॒न त्व॒चम् एतां॒ विशस्तर् यथापर्व् अ॑सि॒ना मा॒भि॒ मंस्थाः । मा॒भि॒ द्रुहः परुशः॒ कल्पयैनं तृती॒ये ना॒के अ॒धि वि॒ श्रयैनम् ॥४॥
9.5.e: Cut up this skin with the grey knife, Dissector! dividing joint from joint, and mangle nothing Do him no injury: limb by limb arrange him, and send him up to the third cope of heaven.

9.5.d: ऋचा॒ कुम्भी॒म् अ॒ध्य् अग्नौ॒ श्रयाम्य् आ॒ सिञ्चोदक॒म् अ॒व धेह्य् एनम् । पर्या॒धत्ताग्नि॒ना शमितारः शृतो॒ गछतु सुकृ॒तां य॒त्र लोकः॒ ॥५॥
9.5.e: With verse upon the fire I set the caldron: pour in the water; lay him down within it! Encompass him with fire, ye Immolators. Cooked, let him reach the world where dwell the righteous.

9.5.d: उ॒त् क्रामा॒तः प॒रि चेद् अ॒तप्तस् तप्ता॒च् चरो॒र् अ॒धि ना॒कं तृती॒यम् । अग्ने॒र् अग्नि॒र् अ॒धि सं॒ बभूविथ ज्यो॒तिष्मन्तम् अभि॒ लोकं॒ जयैत॒म् ॥६॥
9.5.e: Hence come thou forth, vexed by no pain or torment. Mount to the third heaven from the heated vessel. As fire out of the fire hast thou arisen. Conquer and win this lucid world of splendour.

9.5.d: अजो॒ अग्नि॒र् अज॒म् उ ज्यो॒तिर् आहुर् अजं॒ जी॒वता ब्रह्म॒णे दे॒यम् आहुः । अज॒स् त॒मांस्य् अ॒प हन्ति दूर॒म् अस्मिं॒ल् लोके॒ श्रद्द॒धानेन दत्तः॒ ॥७॥
9.5.e: The Goat is Agni: light they call him, saying that living man must give him to the Brāhman. Given in this world by a devout believer, the Goat dispels and drives afar the darkness.

9.5.d: प॒ञ्चौदनः पञ्चधा॒ वि॒ क्रमताम् आक्रंस्य॒मानस् त्री॒णि ज्यो॒तींषि । ईजाना॒नां सुकृ॒तां प्रे॒हि म॒ध्यं तृती॒ये ना॒के अ॒धि वि॒ श्रयस्व ॥८॥
9.5.e: Let the Panchaudana Goat, about to visit the three lights, pass away in five divisions. Go midst the pious who have paid their worship, and parted, dwell on the third cope of heaven.

9.5.d: अ॒जा॒ रोह सुकृ॒तां य॒त्र लोकः॒ शरभो॒ न॒ चत्तो॒ ऽति दुर्गा॒न्य् एषः । प॒ञ्चौदनो ब्रह्म॒णे दीय॒मानः स॒ दाता॒रं तृ॒प्त्या तर्पयाति ॥९॥
9.5.e: Rise to that world, O Goat, where dwell the righteous: pass, like a Sarabha veiled, all difficult places. The Goat Panchaudana, given to a Brāhman, shall with all ful- ness satisfy the giver.

9.5.d: अज॒स् त्रिनाके॒ त्रिदिवे॒ त्रिपृष्ठे॒ ना॒कस्य पृष्ठे॒ ददिवां॒सं दधाति । प॒ञ्चौदनो ब्रह्म॒णे दीय॒मानो विश्व॒रूपा धेनुः॒ कामदु॒घास्य् ए॒का ॥१०॥ {११}
9.5.e: The Goat Panchaudana, given to a Brāhman, sets the bestower on the pitch of heaven, In the third vault, third sky, third ridge. One only Cow omni- form art thou, that yields all wishes.

9.5.d: एत॒द् वो ज्यो॒तिः पितरस् तृती॒यं प॒ञ्चौदनं ब्रह्म॒णे ऽजं॒ ददाति । अज॒स् त॒मांस्य् अ॒प हन्ति दूर॒म् अस्मिं॒ल् लोके॒ श्रद्द॒धानेन दत्तः॒ ॥११॥
9.5.e: That is the third light that is yours, ye Fathers. He gives the Goat Panchaudana to the Brāhman. Given in this world by the devout believer, the Goat dispels and drives afar the darkness.

9.5.d: ईजाना॒नां सुकृ॒तां लोक॒म् ई॒प्सन् प॒ञ्चौदनं ब्रह्म॒णे ऽजं॒ ददाति । स॒ व्या॑प्तिम् अभि॒ लोकं॒ जयैतं॒ शिवो॑ ऽस्म॒भ्यं प्र॒तिगृहीतो अस्तु ॥१२॥
9.5.e: Seeking the world of good men who have worshipped, he gives the Goat Panchaudana to the Brāhman. Win thou this world as thy complete possession. Auspicious unto us be he, accepted!

9.5.d: अजो॒ ह्य् अ॑ग्ने॒र् अ॒जनिष्ट शो॒काद् वि॒प्रो वि॒प्रस्य स॒हसो विपश्चि॒त् । इष्टं॒ पूर्त॒म् अभि॒पूर्तं व॒षट्कृतं त॒द् देवा॒ ऋतुशः॒ कल्पयन्तु ॥१३॥
9.5.e: Truly the Goat sprang from the glow of Agni, inspired as sage with all a sage's power. Sacrifice, filled, filled full, offered with Vashat—this let the Gods arrange.at proper seasons.

9.5.d: अमोतं॒ वा॒सो दद्याद् धि॒रण्यम् अ॒पि द॒क्षिणाम् । त॒था लोका॒न्त् स॒म् आप्नोति ये॒ दिव्या॒ ये॒ च पा॒र्थिवाः ॥१४॥
9.5.e: Home-woven raiment let him give, and gold as guerdon to the priests. So he obtains completely all celestial and terrestrial worlds.

9.5.d: एता॒स् त्वाजो॒प यन्तु धा॒राः सोम्या॒ देवी॒र् घृत॒पृष्ठा मधुश्चु॒तः । स्तभान् पृथिवी॒म् उत॒ द्यां॒ ना॒कस्य पृष्ठे॒ ऽधि सप्त॒रश्मौ ॥१५॥
9.5.e: Near to thee, Goat! approach these streams of Soma, divine, distilling meath, bedecked with butter! Stay thou the earth and sky and fix them firmly up on the seven- rayed pitch and height of heaven.

9.5.d: अजो॒ ऽस्य् अ॒ज स्वर्गो॒ ऽसि त्व॒या लोक॒म् अ॒ङ्गिरसः प्रा॒जानन् । तं॒ लोकं॒ पु॒ण्यं प्र॒ ज्ञेषम् ॥१६॥
9.5.e: Unborn art thou, O Goat: to heaven thou goest. Though thee Angirases knew that radiant region. So may I know that holy world.

9.5.d: ये॒ना सह॒स्रं व॒हसि ये॒नाग्ने सर्ववेदस॒म् । ते॒नेमं॒ यज्ञं॒ नो वह स्व॑र् देवे॒षु ग॒न्तवे ॥१७॥
9.5.e: Convey our sacrifice to heaven, that it may reach the Gods, with that Whereby thou, Agni, bearest wealth in thousands, and all pre- cious things.

9.5.d: अजः॒ पक्वः॒ स्वर्गे॒ लोके॒ दधाति प॒ञ्चौदनो नि॒रृतिं बा॒धमानः । ते॒न लोका॒न्त् सू॒र्यवतो जयेम ॥१८॥
9.5.e: The Goat Panchaudana, when cooked, transporteth, repelling Nirriti, to the world of Svarga. By him may we win worlds which Sūrya brightens.

9.5.d: यं॒ ब्राह्मणे॒ निदधे॒ यं॒ च विक्षु॒ या॒ विप्रु॒ष ओदना॒नाम् अज॒स्य । स॒र्वं त॒द् अग्ने सुकृत॒स्य लोके॒ जानीता॒न् नः संग॒मने पथीना॒म् ॥१९॥
9.5.e: The droppings of the Odanas attending the Goat which I have lodged with priest or people May all this know us in the world of virtue, O Agni, at the meeting of the pathways.

9.5.d: अजो॒ वा॒ इद॒म् अग्ने व्य् अ॑क्रमत त॒स्यो॒र इय॒म् अभवद् द्यौः॒ पृष्टिह॒म् । अन्त॒रिक्षं म॒ध्यम् दि॒शः पार्श्वे॒ समुद्रौ॒ कुक्षी॒ ॥२०॥ {१२}
9.5.e: This Unborn cleft apart in the beginning: his breast became the earth, his back was heaven. His middle was the air, his sides the regions; the hollows of his belly formed both oceans.

9.5.d: सत्यं॒ च र्तं॒ च च॒क्षुषी वि॒श्वं सत्यं॒ श्रद्धा॒ प्राणो॒ विरा॒ट् शि॒रः । एष॒ वा॒ अ॒परिमितो यज्ञो॒ य॒द् अजः॒ प॒ञ्चौदनः ॥२१॥
9.5.e: His eyes were Truth and Right. The whole together was Truth: Virāj his head and Faith his breathing. This Goat Panchaudana was indeed a sacrifice unlimited.

9.5.d: अ॒परिमितम् एव॒ यज्ञ॒म् आप्नो॒त्य् अ॒परिमितं लोक॒म् अ॒व रुन्द्धे । यो॑ ऽजं॒ प॒ञ्चौदनं द॒क्षिणाज्योतिषं द॒दाति ॥२२॥
9.5.e: A boundless sacrifice he performs, he wins himself a boundless world: Who gives the Goat Panchaudana illumined with a priestly fee.

9.5.d: ना॒स्या॒स्थीनि भिन्द्यान् न॒ मज्ज्ञो॒ नि॒र् धयेत् । स॒र्वम् एनं समादा॒येद॒मिदं प्र॒ वेशयेत् ॥२३॥
9.5.e: Let him not break the victim's bones, let him not suck the marrow out. Let the man, taking him entire, here, even here deposit him.

9.5.d: इद॒मिदम् एवा॒स्य रूपं॒ भवति ते॒नैनं सं॒ गमयति । इ॒षं म॒ह ऊ॒र्जम् अस्मै दुहे यो॑ ऽजं॒ प॒ञ्चौदनम् द॒क्षिणाज्योतिषं द॒दाति ॥२४॥
9.5.e: This, even this is his true form: the man uniteth him therewith. Food, greatness, strength he bringeth him who giveth the Goat Panchaudana illumed with guerdon.

9.5.d: प॒ञ्च रुक्मा॒ प॒ञ्च न॒वानि व॒स्त्रा प॒ञ्चास्मै धेन॒वः कामदु॒घा भवन्ति । यो॑ ऽजं॒ प॒ञ्चौदनं द॒क्षिणाज्योतिषं द॒दाति ॥२५॥
9.5.e: The five gold pieces, and the five new garments, and the five milch-kine yield him all his wishes. Who gives the Goat Panchaudana illumined with a priestly fee.

9.5.d: प॒ञ्च रुक्मा॒ ज्यो॒तिर् अस्मै भवन्ति व॒र्म वा॒सांसि तन्वे॑ भवन्ति । स्वर्गं॒ लोक॒म् अश्नुते यो॑ ऽजं॒ प॒ञ्चौदनं द॒क्षिणाज्योतिषम् द॒दाति ॥२६॥
9.5.e: The five gold pieces, area light to light him, robes become armour to defend his body; He winneth Svarga as his home who giveth the Goat Panchaud- ana illumed with bountry.

9.5.d: या॒ पू॒र्वं प॒तिं वित्त्वा॒ ऽथान्यं॒ विन्द॒ते॒ ऽपरम् । प॒ञ्चौदनं च ता॒व् अजं॒ द॒दातो न॒ वि॒ योषतः ॥२७॥
9.5.e: When she who hath been wedded finds a second husband after- ward, The twain shall not be parted if they give the Goat Panchaud- ana.

9.5.d: समान॒लोको भवति पुनर्भु॒वा॒परः प॒तिः । यो॑ ऽजं॒ प॒ञ्चौदनम् द॒क्षिणाज्योतिषं द॒दाति ॥२८॥
9.5.e: One world with the re-wedded wife becomes the second hus- band's home. Who gives the Goat Panchaudana illumined with the priestly fee.

9.5.d: अनुपूर्व॒वत्सां धेनु॒म् अनड्वा॒हम् उपब॒र्हणम् । वा॒सो हि॒रण्यं दत्त्वा॒ ते॒ यन्ति दि॒वम् उत्तमा॒म् ॥२९॥
9.5.e: They who have given a cow who drops a calf each season, or an ox, A coverlet, a robe, or gold, go to the loftiest sphere of heaven.

9.5.d: आत्मा॒नं पित॒रं पुत्रं॒ पौ॒त्रं पितामह॒म् । जायां॒ ज॒नित्रीं मात॒रं ये॒ प्रिया॒स् ता॒न् उ॒प ह्वये ॥३०॥ {१३}
9.5.e: Himself, the father and the son, the grandson, and the father's sire, Mother, wife, her who bore his babes, all the beloved ones I call.

9.5.d: यो॒ वै॒ नै॒दाघं ना॒म र्तुं॒ वे॒द । एष॒ वै॒ नै॒दाघो ना॒म र्तु॒र् य॒द् अजः॒ प॒ञ्चौदनः । नि॒र् एवा॒प्रियस्य भ्रा॒तृव्यस्य श्रि॒यं दहति भ॒वत्य् आत्म॒ना ।
9.5.e: The man who knows the season named the Scorching—the Goat Pafichaudana is this scorching season He lives himself, he verily burns up his hated rival's fame, Who gives the Goat Panchaudana illumined with the priestly fee.

9.5.d: यो॒ वै॒ कुर्व॒न्तं ना॒म र्तुं॒ वे॒द । कुर्वतीं॒कुर्वतीम् एवा॒प्रियस्य भ्रा॒तृव्यस्य श्रि॒यं आ॒ दत्ते । एष॒ वै॒ कुर्व॒न् ना॒म र्तु॒र् य॒द् अजः॒ प॒ञ्चौदनः ।
9.5.e: The man who knows the season called the Working takes to himself the active fame, his hated rival's active fame. The Goat Panchaudana is this Working season. He lives himself, etc.

9.5.d: यो॒ वै॒ संय॒न्तं ना॒म र्तुं॒ वे॒द । संयतीं॒संयतीम् एवा॒प्रियस्य भ्रा॒तृव्यस्य श्रि॒यं आ॒ दत्ते । एष॒ वै॒ संय॒न् ना॒म र्तु॒र् य॒द् अजः॒ प॒ञ्चौदनः ।
9.5.e: The man who knows the season called the Meeting takes to him- self the gathering fame, his hated rival's gathering fame. The Goat Panchaudana is this Meeting season.

9.5.d: यो॒ वै॒ पिन्व॒न्तं ना॒म र्तु॒म् वे॒द । पिन्वतीं॒पिन्वतीम् एवा॒प्रियस्य भ्रा॒तृव्यस्य श्रि॒यं आ॒ दत्ते । एष॒ वै॒ पिन्व॒न् ना॒म र्तु॒र् य॒द् अजः॒ प॒ञ्चौदनः ।
9.5.e: The man who knows the called the Swelling takes to himself the swelling fame, his hated rival's swelling fame. The Goat Panchaudana is this Swelling season. He lives himself, etc.

9.5.d: यो॒ वा॒ उद्य॒न्तं ना॒म र्तुं॒ वे॒द । उद्यतीं॒उद्यतीम् एवा॒प्रियस्य भ्रा॒तृव्यस्य श्रि॒यं आ॒ दत्ते । एष॒ वा॒ उद्य॒न्न् ना॒म र्तु॒र् य॒द् अजः॒ प॒ञ्चौदनः ।
9.5.e: The man who knows the season called the Rising takes to him- self the rising fame, his hated rival's rising fame. The Goat Panchaudana in this Rising season.

9.5.d: यो॒ वा॒ अभिभु॒वं ना॒म र्तुं॒ वे॒द । अभिभ॒वन्तीमभिभवन्तीम् एवा॒प्रियस्य भ्रा॒तृव्यस्य श्रि॒यं आ॒ दत्ते । एष॒ वा॒ अभिभू॒र् ना॒म र्तु॒र् य॒द् अजः॒ प॒ञ्चौदनः ।
9.5.e: The man who knows the season called Surpassing takes to him- self thé conquering fame, his hated rival's conquering fame. The Goat Panchaudana is this Conquering season. He lives himself, he verily burns up his hated rival's fame Who gives the Goat Panchaudana illumined with a priestly fee.

9.5.d: अजं॒ च प॒चत प॒ञ्च चौदना॒न् । स॒र्वा दि॒शः सं॒मनसः सध्री॒चीः सा॒न्तर्देशाः प्र॒ति गृह्न॒न्तु त एत॒म् ॥३७॥
9.5.e: He cooks the Goat and the five boiled rice messes. May the uni- ted Quarters, all accordant, and intermediate points, accept him from thee.

9.5.d: ता॒स् ते रक्षन्तु त॒व तु॒भ्यम् एतं॒ ताभ्य आ॒ज्यं हवि॒र् इदं॒ जुहोमि ॥३८॥ {१४}
9.5.e: May these preserve him for thee. Here I offer t o these the molten butter as oblation.
